Description: This method verifies that the currently running Java version meets the compatibility requirements for eXist-db. If the Java version is not compatible, it will throw a `StartException`.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method checks if the current Java version is compatible with the system's requirements. If an incompatible version is detected, it throws an exception indicating the issue and the detected runtime Java version.
Return value description: This method does not return any value. It either completes successfully or throws a StartException.

Description: This method takes an optional string representing a Java version and extracts its numerical components. It handles different version separators like periods, underscores, and hyphens, and gracefully ignores non-numerical parts.
Return value description: An optional array of integers, where each integer is a numerical component of the Java version. Returns an empty optional if the input string is empty, invalid, or contains no numerical components.

Description: This method constructs an object representing an incompatible Java version, specifying the required major version and optional constraints for minor and patch versions.
Return value description: An `IncompatibleJavaVersion` object that details the specific Java version requirements.

Description: Creates an instance representing an incompatible Java version requirement.
Return value description: An `IncompatibleJavaVersion` object detailing the required major and optional minor version.

Description: This method creates a new instance of an IncompatibleJavaVersion object, initializing it with a specified major version number.
Return value description: A new IncompatibleJavaVersion object representing an incompatible Java version with the provided major version.

Description: This method attempts to add a component to the system, represented by a string. It validates the input string to ensure it's not null or empty before proceeding to add it.
Return value description: Returns true if the component was successfully added, and false otherwise. This includes cases where the input is invalid or the addition process fails.

Description: This method adds a valid and existing file system path to a collection of class path elements, ensuring no duplicates are added.
Return value description: Returns true if the path was successfully added to the collection, and false otherwise (if the path was null, did not exist, or was already present).

Description: This method processes a string representing a file path separator-delimited classpath and adds each individual classpath component to a collection.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method provides an iterator for accessing the elements within the class path.
Return value description: An iterator that allows sequential access to the class path elements.

Description: This method iterates through a provided classpath and adds each resulting URL to a collection of URLs that can be used for loading resources.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method dynamically executes the `main` method of a specified class using a given class loader and arguments, allowing one Java program to launch another.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method serves as the entry point for the application. It initializes and runs the main application logic, handling any uncaught exceptions by printing them to the console and exiting with an error code.
Return value description: The method returns `void` as it does not explicitly return any value. Its primary purpose is to execute application logic and manage program termination.

Description: This method initiates the eXist-db database by calling a startup routine. If the startup fails, it prints an error message and exits the program with a specific error code.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.
Technique 2: Exits the application with a specific error code.

Description: This method initializes and starts the eXist-db application. It performs checks for Java compatibility, sets up logging, and configures the runtime environment based on command-line arguments, potentially invoking a specified main class using a custom class loader.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method performs a clean shutdown of the eXist-db database by stopping all associated broker pools. It is primarily intended for use within test environments.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.
Technique 1: Reflection is used to access and invoke private methods of the eXist-db internal classes.

Description: This method compiles and resolves an XSLT stylesheet. It handles stylesheet caching based on provided properties and a base URI. If caching is enabled and no properties are provided, it uses a simplified resolution method. Otherwise, it creates a new StylesheetResolverAndCompiler instance with the stylesheet URI and properties.
Return value description: A Stylesheet object representing the compiled and resolved XSLT stylesheet.

Description: This method resolves and potentially compiles an XSLT stylesheet. It can either retrieve a cached version of the stylesheet or create a new stylesheet resolver and compiler.
Return value description: A Stylesheet object representing the resolved and compiled stylesheet.

Description: This method generates a Stylesheet object that can be used to transform XML documents. It configures a SAX transformer factory and sets up a URI resolver to handle external resources during the transformation process. The returned Stylesheet object provides methods to create Templates and TransformerHandlers, which are core components for applying XSLT transformations.
Return value description: A Stylesheet object containing nested methods to generate XML transformation templates and transformer handlers, utilizing a pre-configured SAX transformer factory and URI resolver.

Description: This method compiles XSLT stylesheets from a database broker and returns them as a `Templates` object. It handles potential errors during the compilation process.
Return value description: A `Templates` object representing the compiled XSLT stylesheets, ready for use in transformations.

Description: This method creates a TransformerHandler, which is used to apply XSL transformations to XML documents. It allows for custom error handling during the transformation process and ensures that the user has the necessary permissions.
Return value description: Returns a TransformerHandler that can be used to perform XSL transformations with specified error handling and security constraints.

Description: This method compiles and returns XSLT templates. It first checks if the templates have already been compiled and if the underlying stylesheet resource has been modified. If not, it proceeds to compile the stylesheet from either an embedded XML database resource or a remote URL.
Return value description: Returns the compiled XSLT templates.
Technique 2: File system access (reading remote stylesheet URLs)

Description: This method creates and returns a TransformerHandler configured with XSLT templates and an error listener. It retrieves templates based on the provided database broker and ensures that any transformation errors are reported to the specified listener. The transformer's error listener is also explicitly set for error reporting during transformations.
Return value description: A configured TransformerHandler instance that can be used to apply XSLT transformations.
Technique 1: Database call: Interacts with a DBBroker to retrieve configuration or data.
Technique 2: XSLT processing: Utilizes XSLT templates for transformation.
Technique 3: Error handling: Configures an error listener for reporting transformation issues.

Description: This method is responsible for reporting an error that occurred during a transformation process. It takes a descriptive error message and the original exception as input.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method checks for different types of errors (WARNING, ERROR, FATAL) reported during an XSL transformation and raises them if configured to stop on those error types. It provides details about the error message and its location.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.
Technique 1: Conditional logic based on error type and configuration settings (stopOnWarn, stopOnError).

Description: This method logs an XSL transform warning, records the warning as an error type, stores the exception, and optionally re-throws the exception if configured to stop on warnings.

This method handles recoverable errors during an XSL transformation. It logs the error, updates the error type and exception state, and optionally re-throws the exception if the transformation is configured to stop on error.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method handles a fatal error encountered during an XSL transformation. It logs the error, records the error type and exception, and then re-throws the original exception to be handled by the calling process.

This method parses an XML document from an eXist-db input source and processes it using SAX handlers. It serializes the document content and sends the SAX events to a content handler. Error handling is included for parsing exceptions.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method is intended to parse data associated with a given system identifier, but currently, it is not implemented and will throw an exception if called.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method resolves a given uniform resource identifier (URI) or relative path, considering a base URI, to produce a source for processing. It handles various URI formats, including absolute, root-relative, and embedded server paths, constructing a final path for either a database lookup or a URL-based source.
Return value description: Returns a `Source` object, which represents the resolved resource, either from a database or a URL.

Description: This method creates a new collection within the system, delegating the actual creation to another method that accepts additional parameters.
Return value description: The method returns a boolean indicating whether the collection was successfully created.

Description: This method creates a new collection with a given name and creation date. It handles potential errors related to URI syntax by re-throwing them as an EXistException.
Return value description: Returns true if the collection was successfully created, and false otherwise.

Description: Configures a collection within the eXist-db database by translating the collection name to a URI and then calling an internal configuration method. This operation may throw exceptions related to eXist-db errors or permission denials.
Return value description: Returns true if the collection was successfully configured, and false otherwise.

Description: This method generates a unique identifier for a given collection name by constructing a database URI.
Return value description: A string representing the generated unique identifier.

Description: This method executes a compiled XQuery against a database broker, returning the results of the query. It handles query execution, potential errors, and manages document locking during the process.
Return value description: The method returns a QueryResult object containing either the successful results of the XQuery execution and output properties, or an XPathException if an error occurred.

Description: This method attempts to lock all documents within a specified collection for protected access, retrying the operation if deadlocks are encountered.
Return value description: A map containing documents that have been successfully locked for protected access, or null if protected mode is not specified.
Technique 1: Database call to open and read collection documents.
Technique 2: Database locking mechanism for documents and collections.

Description: This method executes a given query against a database, compiles it, and returns a diagnostic dump of the compiled query. It handles potential exceptions related to database operations and permissions.
Return value description: A string representing the diagnostic dump of the compiled query.

Description: This method inspects an XQuery's pragmas to identify serialization settings and applies them to the current output properties if found.
Technique 1: Retrieving options from a context object

Description: This method processes pragma options, extracting key-value pairs from their content and storing them in a provided map. It handles null pragmas and invalid parameter formats by either returning or throwing an exception. Debugging information is logged when a pragma property is set.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method executes a query against the eXist database after converting an XPath expression from bytes to a String using the specified encoding. It logs the query if debug logging is enabled and then delegates the execution to another method.
Return value description: The method returns an integer representing the result of the database query, likely indicating the number of documents found or modified.

Description: This method executes an XPath query against a database, handling potential errors and measuring the query execution time. It then adds the query results to a cache.
Return value description: The method returns an integer representing the index of the added query result in the cache.

Description: This method checks if a specified collection URI points to an existing collection that the current user has permission to open. It validates the URI format and then attempts to open the collection with a read lock. If the collection exists and can be opened, it returns true; otherwise, it throws an exception indicating a URI syntax error, the collection not existing, or insufficient permissions.

This method retrieves a description of a specified resource. It handles potential errors related to resource lookup and URI syntax.  It makes a call to another method to perform the actual description retrieval.
This method retrieves a description of a specified collection within the eXist-db database. It handles cases where the root collection is null by defaulting to the eXist-db root URI.
Return value description: A map containing details about the collection.

Description: This method updates an XML database collection with new XML data, handling potential URI syntax errors.
Return value description: Returns an integer representing the result of the update operation.

Description: This method updates a specified resource with new XML data, handling potential URI syntax errors and security permissions.
Return value description: The method returns an integer representing the success or status code of the update operation.

Description: This method synchronizes the system's data with the database in a major update, handling potential exceptions.
Return value description: Returns true if the synchronization was successful, and false if any exceptions occurred during the process.

Description: This method initiates a system task to perform a data backup to a specified destination. It leverages a factory to access a broker pool and then triggers the data backup process.
Return value description: The method returns a boolean value indicating that the data backup initiation process was successful.

Description: This method generates a unique identifier for a resource within a specified collection.
Return value description: A string representing the unique identifier for the resource.

Description: Retrieves a list of permissions associated with a given document name. This involves translating the document name into a database URI and then querying the database for the permissions.
Return value description: A map where keys are permission categories (e.g., 'read', 'write') and values are lists of users or groups who have that permission for the document.

Description: Retrieves a list of permissions associated with a specified collection. This method acts as a convenience wrapper, converting a collection name into a URI before delegating the actual permission retrieval.
This method removes a group by its name. It may throw exceptions related to database errors or insufficient permissions.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method checks if a document exists at the specified path within the eXist database.
Return value description: Returns true if the document exists, and false otherwise.

Description: Checks if a collection with the given name exists in the eXist-db. It constructs a URI for the collection and then delegates to another method for the actual check.
Return value description: Returns true if the collection exists, and false otherwise.

Description: This method parses an XML byte array and stores it within the eXist-db database, overwriting existing documents if specified.
Return value description: Returns true if the XML was successfully parsed and stored, and false otherwise.

Description: This method parses XML data, taking into account the document's path, MIME type, and an overwrite flag. It then delegates the parsing to another method with additional parameters.
Return value description: The method returns a boolean indicating whether the parsing process was successful.

Description: This method parses XML data, optionally overwriting existing documents in a specified path, and records creation and modification timestamps. It acts as a simplified entry point for parsing XML content by delegating to another method with additional parameters.
Return value description: Returns a boolean indicating whether the parsing operation was successful. True indicates success, and false indicates failure.

Description: This method stores an XML document in a specified path within a collection. It handles cases where the document already exists, either by throwing an exception if overwriting is not permitted or by proceeding with the storage if overwriting is allowed. It also logs the time taken to store the document.
Return value description: Returns true if the document was successfully stored, and false otherwise.
Technique 1: Database call to store a document.
Technique 2: Database call to acquire a document write lock.
Technique 3: Database call to retrieve a document if it already exists.

Description: This method parses a locally stored file that was previously uploaded. It handles overwriting existing files and validates the file's mime type. The temporary file used for parsing is removed after processing. This operation may involve database interactions for storing or validating file metadata and permissions checks.
Return value description: The method returns true if the file is considered valid after parsing, and false otherwise.

Description: This method parses a locally uploaded file, treating it as either XML or binary, and saves it to a specified document path. It handles overwriting existing files and ensures the temporary file is removed after processing. The method validates the file's format and the user's permissions before proceeding.
Return value description: Returns true if the file is successfully parsed and considered valid, otherwise false.

Description: This method parses a local file and stores it as an XML document. It handles potential overwriting of existing documents and sets metadata such as MIME type, creation date, and modification date. It also validates the document path.
Return value description: Returns true if the parsing and storage were successful, and false otherwise.

Description: This method processes a local file, parses it, and stores it within the eXist database. It handles potential overwrites and uses provided metadata such as MIME type, creation, and modification dates.
Return value description: Returns a boolean indicating whether the parsing and storage operation was successful.

Description: Stores binary data in a specified document path, with options for overwriting and potentially handling related metadata. This operation may involve interactions with a document store.
Return value description: Returns true if the binary data was successfully stored, and false otherwise.

Description: This method stores binary data into a document repository, identified by its path and MIME type. It allows for optional overwriting of existing documents and associates creation and modification dates with the stored data. This operation may throw exceptions related to URI syntax, repository errors, or permission issues.
Return value description: Returns true if the binary data was successfully stored, and false otherwise.

Description: This method handles the upload of data chunks, either creating a new temporary file or appending to an existing one. It supports both compressed and uncompressed data, writing the processed data to the appropriate file.
Return value description: The method returns the name or handle of the file where the data was written.
Technique 1: File I/O operations (writing to a file)

Description: This method generates an XML representation of a sequence of items, processing a specified range and handling different item types. It constructs the XML output based on provided properties and metadata about the sequence, such as hit count, starting position, and the number of items to include. The method also handles cases where the input sequence is empty or parameters are out of range.
Return value description: The method returns an XML string representing the processed sequence of items. This XML includes metadata like the total hit count, the starting position, and the number of items returned, along with the serialized items themselves. If the input sequence is empty, it returns a minimal XML structure indicating zero hits.

Description: This method compiles an XQuery query provided as a string, processing it with given parameters.
Return value description: The method returns a map containing either compilation errors (message, line, and column) or a null value if compilation is successful.

Description: This method executes an XPath query against the database with specified parameters, limiting the number of results and the starting point. It handles potential database exceptions and permission errors during execution. If no results are found, it returns an empty XML document. Otherwise, it formats and returns the query results.
Return value description: An XML string representing the query results, including hit count and namespaces, or an empty XML document if no results are found.
Technique 3: Error handling for database and permission exceptions

Description: This method executes an XPath query against a specified document path, returning results as a map. It serves as a deprecated wrapper, delegating the actual query execution to a more specific method with enhanced error handling and URI management. The query can be parameterized, and permissions are checked before execution.
Return value description: A map containing the results of the XPath query. The specific structure and content of the map depend on the query and the data it retrieves.

Description: This method queries the database using an XQuery and returns the results as a map of strings to objects. It handles potential database exceptions and permission errors.
Return value description: A map containing the query results, keyed by string identifiers.

Description: This method executes an eXist database query using provided XQuery, an optional document name, an optional session ID, and a map of parameters. It handles potential exceptions related to database errors and permissions.
Return value description: The method returns a map of strings to objects, representing the results of the database query.

Description: This method executes a query against a binary document, validating user permissions and resource type before processing the query and returning a response.
Return value description: The method returns a map containing the RPC response from the executed query, which includes the results and any relevant metadata.

Description: This method executes a query against a binary XML document. It first checks if the document exists, is a binary resource, and if the current user has read and execute permissions. Then, it compiles the query, executes it, and returns the results formatted as a map. The execution time is also measured.
Return value description: A map containing the query results, potentially including sorting information.
Technique 1: Database call to read a document.
Technique 2: Database call to compile and execute an XQuery.

Description: This method releases a query result associated with a specific handle. It removes the result from a cache and logs the action if debug logging is enabled.
Return value description: Always returns true, indicating the release operation was performed.

Description: This method removes a query result from the cache based on its handle and hash.
Return value description: The method returns true, indicating that the removal operation was attempted.

Description: This method removes a document from the XML database based on its file path. It handles potential errors during the database operation and permission issues.
Return value description: Returns true if the document was successfully removed, and false otherwise.

Description: This method initiates the removal of a collection by first creating a URI for the collection and then calling another method to perform the actual removal.
Return value description: The method returns a boolean indicating whether the collection was successfully removed.

Description: This method removes a user account from the system, provided the current user has administrative privileges.
Return value description: Returns true if the account removal was successful, otherwise an exception is thrown.

Description: Retrieves a document as a byte array by first fetching its content as an XML string and then encoding it based on provided parameters.
Return value description: A byte array representing the content of the requested document.

Description: Retrieves a document as a string from a database using its path, a document identifier, and optional parameters. This operation may involve database interactions and security checks.
Return value description: A string representation of the requested document.

Description: This method retrieves the first chunk of a document, optionally compressing it, and returns it along with metadata indicating whether the entire document was sent or if a handle is available for further retrieval. It handles document serialization and manages temporary file resources for storing the document chunk. If the document exceeds a certain size, a handle is provided for subsequent chunk retrieval. It also manages temporary file resources and potentially caches results for future use.
Return value description: A map containing the first chunk of the document as a byte array under the key 'data', an offset indicating where this chunk ends, and optionally a 'handle' and 'supports-long-offset' boolean if the document is large and requires further retrieval.

Description: This method retrieves data based on a result ID and a number, returning it as a byte array, optionally compressed. It first obtains the data as an XML string and then either compresses it or directly converts it to bytes using the specified encoding.
Return value description: A byte array representing the requested data, which may be compressed.

Description: This method retrieves a chunk of data from a query result. It handles serialization of XML nodes or direct retrieval of string values, and optionally compresses the output. If the data exceeds a certain size, it's cached and a handle is returned; otherwise, the temporary file is released. The method returns the first chunk of data, a handle for further retrieval if applicable, and an offset.
Return value description: A map containing the first chunk of data as bytes, an optional handle for accessing subsequent chunks if the data is large, and an offset indicating the start of the next chunk.
Technique 1: Database call (to retrieve query result and item)
Technique 2: File I/O (writing to a temporary file)

Description: Retrieves all data associated with a given result identifier, using provided parameters, and returns it as a byte array.
Return value description: A byte array representing all the data for the specified result.
Technique 1: Internal data retrieval (likely to a database or data store)

Description: This method retrieves the initial portion of a query result set, serializing it into XML format. It handles compression, writes the data to a temporary file, and determines if the result set is too large to be returned in a single chunk, providing a handle for subsequent retrieval if necessary.
Return value description: A map containing the first chunk of data as a byte array, an optional handle for retrieving the rest of the data if it exceeds a certain size, and an offset indicating the start of the next chunk.
Technique 1: Database call (to retrieve query result set)

Description: Changes the group ownership of a specified resource within the eXist-db database.

Changes the owner of a specified resource within the database. This operation involves interacting with the database to modify resource ownership and may throw exceptions related to database errors or insufficient permissions.
Return value description: Returns true if the ownership change operation was attempted. It does not indicate success of the operation itself, only that the attempt was made.

Description: Changes the owner and/or group of a specified resource within the database.

This method creates a new user account with specified credentials, group memberships, status, and metadata. It first checks if the account already exists and if the current user has the necessary administrative privileges to create a new account. If these checks pass, it proceeds to construct and configure the user account object before persisting it. The method also handles optional fields like enabled status, user mask, and metadata, which can be provided to customize the new account.
Return value description: The method returns true, indicating that the account creation process was initiated successfully. However, the actual success of the database operation is not reflected in this return value.

Description: This method updates an existing user account with the provided credentials and group memberships, potentially delegating to a more detailed update process.
Return value description: Returns true if the account update was successful, and false otherwise.

Description: This method updates an existing user account with new credentials, group memberships, and metadata. It handles password changes, group assignments, enabling/disabling the account, setting user masks, and updating custom metadata attributes, ensuring proper schema type validation for metadata.
Return value description: Returns true to indicate that the account update operation has been initiated.

Description: This method adds a new group to the system if it does not already exist, provided the current user has the necessary administrative privileges. It processes provided metadata to configure the new group.
Return value description: Returns true if the group was successfully added, and false if a group with the given name already exists.

Description: This method updates an existing group with new managers and metadata. It first checks if the group exists, then adds managers and sets metadata values. Finally, it persists these changes to the database.
Return value description: Returns true if the group was updated successfully, and false if the group does not exist.

Description: This method adds an existing account to a specified group. It first retrieves the account and then associates it with the given group before persisting the changes.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Database call to retrieve an account.
Technique 2: Database call to update an account.

Description: This method adds an existing account as a manager to a specified group within the system.
This method removes a specified user account as a manager from a given group.
This method removes a member from a specified group by updating the member's account information in the security manager.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method updates a user account by adding them to specified groups. If the user account does not exist, it is created. The operation is performed within a database transaction and relies on a security manager to enforce access policies.
Return value description: Returns true if the account update was successful, and false otherwise.

Description: This method updates a user's account by removing them from a specified group and then saving the changes. It handles potential exceptions during the process.
Return value description: The method returns true if the account update and group removal were successful, and false otherwise.
Technique 1: Database call to retrieve and update account information.
Technique 2: Security policy enforcement for user permissions.

Description: This method attempts to acquire a lock on a document identified by its path and the username of the user requesting the lock. It acts as a convenience wrapper for a method that takes a more specific URI object.
Return value description: Returns true if the lock was successfully acquired, and false otherwise.

Description: Checks if a user has a lock on a specific document path.
Return value description: Returns a string indicating the lock status.

Description: This method attempts to unlock a resource located at a specified document path. It delegates the actual unlocking operation to another method after converting the document path into a specific URI format.
Return value description: Returns a boolean indicating whether the resource was successfully unlocked.
Technique 1: Data Transformation: Converts a document path string into a specific URI object.
Technique 2: Internal Method Call: Invokes another method within the same class to perform the core logic.

Description: This method retrieves and aggregates summary information from an XML data store based on a provided XPath query. It processes the query results to determine document counts and node counts within the specified XML structure.
Return value description: A map containing summary statistics, including document counts, node counts, and query execution time.

Description: This method retrieves and summarizes the results of a previously executed query. It checks if the result set exists, updates its access time, and if the results are available, it processes them to generate summary counts of node types and document types. If the results are not available, it returns a summary indicating no results.
Return value description: A map containing summary information about the query results, including the query execution time, raw result data (if available), node counts, and document type counts.

Description: This method increments an internal counter by one.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method increments a counter. It does not interact with any external systems or databases.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method moves or copies a resource from one path to another, potentially renaming it in the process. It handles exceptions related to database operations, permissions, and URI syntax.
Return value description: Returns true if the move or copy operation was successful, and false otherwise.

Description: This method facilitates the movement or copying of a resource from one location to another, with the option to rename it during the process. It supports preserving specific resource attributes based on the provided `PreserveType`.
Return value description: Returns `true` if the resource was successfully moved or copied, and `false` otherwise.

Description: This method either moves or copies a collection from one location to another, optionally renaming it during the operation. It acts as a convenience wrapper for a more detailed method, abstracting away the URI construction.
Return value description: Returns a boolean indicating the success or failure of the move or copy operation.

Description: This method moves or copies a collection from one location to another, optionally renaming it in the process. It handles the preservation of collection properties based on the provided type.
Return value description: Returns true if the operation was successful, false otherwise.

Description: This method initiates the reindexing process for a specified XML database collection.
This method reindexes a specific document within the database. It acquires a read lock on the document, performs the reindexing operation, and logs a debug message upon successful completion.
Return value description: The method returns true to indicate that the reindexing operation was initiated. However, the actual success or failure of the reindexing operation is determined by exceptions thrown.
Technique 1: Database call (acquiring document lock and reindexing)

Description: This method creates a backup of a specified collection within an eXist-db database to a designated destination directory. It handles potential exceptions related to database operations, file system access, and XML parsing.
Return value description: The method returns 'true' if the backup operation is initiated successfully, indicating that no immediate exceptions occurred during setup. It does not explicitly confirm the completion or success of the backup process itself.

Description: This method copies a resource from a specified document path to a destination path with a new name, preserving default settings.
Return value description: Returns true if the resource was successfully copied, and false otherwise.

Description: This method copies a resource from a specified document path to a new destination path with a new name, while optionally preserving its type. It acts as a convenience wrapper for a more detailed move or copy operation.
Return value description: Returns a boolean indicating whether the resource was successfully copied. True if the copy operation was successful, false otherwise.

Description: This method creates a copy of a specified collection at a new location with an optional new name. It preserves the default settings for collection content during the copy operation.
Return value description: Returns true if the collection was successfully copied, and false otherwise.

Description: This method initiates the copying of a collection from a specified source path to a destination path, optionally renaming it and preserving its type.
Return value description: Returns true if the collection was successfully copied, and false otherwise.

Description: This method moves a resource from its current location to a new location with an optional new name.
Return value description: Returns true if the move operation was successful, false otherwise.

Description: This method moves a collection from one location to another and optionally renames it. It handles various exceptions related to database operations and permissions.
Return value description: Returns true if the collection was successfully moved, and false otherwise.

Description: This method recursively copies a collection of documents and sub-collections from a source path to a destination path within a database. It handles nested collections and individual documents, ensuring data integrity through database locks.
Return value description: Returns true if the collection copy operation is successful, indicating that all documents and sub-collections have been duplicated.
Technique 1: Database access for reading and writing documents.
Technique 2: Database locking to ensure consistent data during copy operations.
Technique 3: Recursive function calls to process nested collection structures.

Description: This method updates a specified resource with new XML data, potentially throwing exceptions related to permissions, database errors, or XML parsing issues.
Return value description: The integer value returned by this method is not specified, but it typically indicates the success or result of the update operation.

Description: This method retrieves a summary of a specified result by delegating the call to an internal summary method.

Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method allows for the execution of a given operation on a collection after it has been retrieved and locked.

Description: Configures the API builder to operate on a specific document within a collection by accepting a function that determines the document and its required lock mode.
Return value description: A builder instance configured to proceed with operations involving the specified document and lock mode.
Technique 1: Accepts a functional interface for dynamic document lookup.
Technique 2: Utilizes a tuple to return multiple values (document URI and lock mode).

Description: This method sets up the configuration to execute an operation on a specific document within a collection. It takes a function that determines which document to operate on and its required lock mode.

Description: This method executes a collection operation using a fluent API builder, which involves interacting with an eXist-db. It returns the result of this operation. The operation is performed with a specified collection URI and lock mode.
Return value description: The result of the collection operation, which is expected to be present.

Description: This method provides a way to define and execute an operation on a collection and document after they have been retrieved and locked.
Return value description: A builder object that facilitates the execution of the defined operation.
Technique 1: Execution of a function against retrieved collection and document objects.

Description: This method facilitates the deselection of a collection, enabling subsequent operations without it.
Return value description: A builder instance configured to exclude a collection.

Description: This method removes the current collection from the builder's configuration.
Return value description: A new builder instance is returned, configured without the previously specified collection.

Description: This method executes a collection operation and a combined collection and document operation, returning the results of both.
Return value description: A tuple containing the results of the collection operation as the first element and the results of the collection and document operation as the second element.

Description: This method allows for the execution of a specific operation on a document within a collection. The operation is performed after the document has been retrieved and locked, and the collection has been released.
Return value description: A builder object that facilitates further chaining of operations.

Description: This method orchestrates and executes multiple database operations, including collection-related operations, combined collection and document operations, and individual document operations. It then consolidates and returns the outcomes of these distinct operations.
This method allows an operation to be defined and executed on a document after it has been retrieved and locked, and the collection it belongs to has been released.
Return value description: A builder object that facilitates further fluent API calls to configure the execution of the document operation.

Description: This method executes a collection operation using the FluentBrokerAPI and returns the result. It may throw exceptions related to permissions, locking, or general eXist-db errors.
Return value description: The result of the collection operation.

Description: This method performs a collection operation and a document operation, then returns the results of both.

This method prepares for an operation that will be executed on a Collection and a Document. The operation is guaranteed to run only after both the Collection and Document have been successfully retrieved and locked.
This method is used to remove a collection from the current API builder configuration.
Return value description: A new builder instance with the collection removed.

Description: This method releases a collection, effectively resetting the state to allow for further operations.
Return value description: Returns a new builder instance, allowing for a fluent construction of API calls.

Description: This method performs a collection and document operation, retrieving and returning the result.
This method allows for defining an operation to be performed on a document after it has been retrieved and locked, but before the collection is released.
This method performs a collection and document operation, followed by a document operation, and then returns the combined results.
Return value description: A tuple containing the results of the collection and document operation and the document operation.

Description: This method defines an operation to be performed on a document retrieved from a collection. The operation is executed after the document has been retrieved and locked, and the collection has been released.
Return value description: A builder object that allows for further chained operations, specifically indicating that a document operation has been defined but not yet executed.

Description: This method executes a document operation within the eXist-db system and returns the result of that operation.
This method ensures that a specified data directory exists and is writable, creating it if necessary. It also saves the final data directory path for future use within the system's configuration.
Technique 1: File system operations (checking existence, creating directories, checking writability)

Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Technique 2: Exception handling for lock acquisition and read-only conditions

Description: This method releases a file lock and clears the reference to it.
Return value description: None.

Description: This method prints debugging information about the current lock's state to a specified output stream.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method defines a pointcut for AspectJ that identifies methods annotated with `@EnsureLocked`. It serves to select methods where specific locking logic should be applied.

Description: This method identifies methods annotated with `@EnsureLocked` within the application.
Return value description: It returns a pointcut expression, which is a selector used to match join points in AspectJ programming.

Description: This method defines a pointcut expression for AspectJ. It's used to identify methods annotated with `@EnsureContainerLocked` for aspect-oriented programming, allowing cross-cutting concerns to be applied to those methods.
Return value description: This method does not return any value; its purpose is to define a pointcut.

Description: This code defines a pointcut for AspectJ that matches any method execution where at least one parameter is annotated with `@org.exist.storage.lock.EnsureUnlocked`. This is used to intercept and apply specific behavior to methods designed to ensure a resource is unlocked.
Return value description: This method does not return a value as it is an AspectJ pointcut definition.

Description: This method defines a pointcut for AspectJ, identifying methods annotated with `@EnsureUnlocked`.
Return value description: This method does not return a value; it serves as a configuration for AspectJ.

Description: This method defines a pointcut for AspectJ, specifically targeting methods annotated with `@EnsureContainerUnlocked`. This is used to intercept and apply cross-cutting concerns around container unlocking logic.
Return value description: This method does not return a value; it defines a pointcut configuration.

Description: This method enforces that parameters annotated with `@EnsureLocked` in called methods hold the required locks before proceeding. If the locks are not held and enforcement is enabled, it throws a `LockException`.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.
Technique 1: Aspect-Oriented Programming (AOP) - Before method execution advice
Technique 2: Reflection - Inspecting method signature and parameters
Technique 3: Lock Management - Interacting with a LockManager to check collection and document locks

Description: This method verifies that the returned object from an annotated method is properly locked according to specified requirements. If the locking requirements are not met and enforcement is enabled, it throws an exception.
Return value description: The method does not return a value, but it validates the lock status of the object returned by the intercepted method.
Technique 2: Reflection to inspect method annotations and retrieve method details
Technique 3: Interaction with a LockManager to check lock status on collections or documents

Description: This method enforces lock constraints on a container object before an annotated method is executed. It checks if the required lock is held on either a collection or a document, throwing an exception if the lock is not present and enforcement is enabled.
Return value description: This method does not return a value directly; its purpose is to enforce preconditions through exceptions or by allowing execution to proceed.
Technique 2: Reflection - Accessing method annotations and signatures
Technique 3: Lock Management - Interacting with a LockManager to check collection and document locks

Description: This method enforces a constraint that method parameters annotated with `@EnsureUnlocked` must not hold any locks, either on collections or documents. If a lock is detected and the system is configured to enforce this constraint, a `LockException` is thrown.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.
Technique 1: Aspect-Oriented Programming (AOP) is used to intercept method calls before they execute.
Technique 2: Reflection is used to inspect method signatures and parameter annotations.
Technique 3: A database lock manager is queried to check for existing locks on collections or documents.

Description: This method verifies that no locks are held on a collection or document returned by a method, throwing an exception if locks are found and enforcement is enabled.
Return value description: The return value of the instrumented method is checked for held locks.
Technique 2: Reflection to inspect method annotations and signature

Description: This method enforces that no locks are held on a container object before an instrumented method is called. It checks for locks on collections or documents based on annotations.
Technique 1: Aspect-oriented programming (AOP) is used to intercept method calls.
Technique 2: Reflection is used to inspect method annotations and determine lock types.
Technique 3: A lock manager is accessed to query the status of locks on collections or documents.

Description: Attempts to acquire a read lock on a resource. This method is deprecated and should not be used in new code.
Return value description: Returns true if the lock was successfully acquired, and false otherwise.

Description: This method attempts to obtain a lock, either for reading or writing, to ensure exclusive access to a resource. It will return true if the lock is successfully acquired, and false otherwise. It may throw an exception if there is an issue during the lock acquisition process.
This method tries to obtain a read or write lock. If the lock cannot be acquired immediately, the operation fails and returns false.
Return value description: Returns true if the lock was successfully acquired, and false otherwise.

Description: This method releases a lock previously acquired by the system, based on the specified lock mode.
This method releases a specified number of references for a given lock mode.
This method checks if a resource is currently locked by any active read or write operations.
Return value description: Returns true if an active read or write lock exists on the resource, and false otherwise.

Description: This method determines if a given thread possesses a read or write lock on a resource.
Return value description: Returns true if the specified thread holds a lock on the resource, and false otherwise.

Description: This method is responsible for notifying any threads that are currently waiting and triggering a recalculation of dependencies. It is specifically utilized to re-execute deadlock detection processes.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method generates a human-readable string representation of the current lock table state, detailing both acquired locks and locks that are currently being attempted. It can optionally include stack trace information for debugging purposes.
Return value description: A formatted string representing the state of the lock table, including acquired and attempting locks, with optional stack trace details.

Description: Serializes the current state of the lock table, including acquired and attempting locks, to an XML format. This representation can optionally include stack trace information for each lock owner.
Return value description: This method does not return a value; it writes the XML output to a provided Writer.

Description: This method attempts to acquire a lock in a specified mode. If the lock cannot be acquired, it throws an exception.
Return value description: A lock that is managed to ensure it will be released when its close method is called.

Description: This method attempts to acquire a lock on a given resource in a specified mode and type. If the lock cannot be acquired, it throws an exception.
Return value description: A managed lock object that ensures the acquired lock is automatically released when the object is closed.

Description: This method attempts to acquire a lock in a specified mode. If the lock cannot be acquired, it throws an exception. Otherwise, it returns a managed lock that will automatically be released when closed.
Return value description: A managed lock object that ensures the acquired lock is released, typically through a close operation.
Technique 2: Exception handling for lock acquisition failures

Description: This method acquires a lock in either read or write mode on a provided `ReadWriteLock` object. It ensures that the lock is held before returning.
Return value description: A managed lock object that guarantees the acquired lock will be released when its `close()` method is called.

Description: This method attempts to acquire a lock in either read or write mode. If the lock cannot be acquired, it throws an exception.
Return value description: A managed lock object that will automatically release the lock when its close method is called.

Description: This method acquires a lock, ensuring that only one process can access a shared resource at a time.
Return value description: The method returns a managed lock object that will automatically release the lock when it is no longer needed.

Description: This method attempts to acquire a lock using a non-blocking tryLock operation. If the lock cannot be acquired immediately, it throws an exception.
Return value description: A managed lock object that ensures the lock is released when its 'close' method is called.

Description: This method releases a lock, ensuring it is only executed once. It marks the lock as closed after releasing it.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method stops the lock table processor, preventing any subsequent lock events from being reported.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method records an attempt to acquire a lock on a specific group and resource, noting the type of lock and the desired mode.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: Records an event indicating that an attempt to acquire a lock has failed. This operation logs the failure details, including group, identifier, lock type, and the mode of the lock attempt.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method records an event indicating that a lock has been acquired for a specific group, identified by an ID, with a given lock type and mode.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method records that a lock has been released. It signals a lock event, specifying the group, identifier, lock type, and lock mode involved in the release.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Return value description: Returns the updated or newly created entry.
Technique 3: In-memory data structure operations (likely a hash set or map)

Return value description: The method returns the modified lock entry if the unmerge operation was successful, otherwise it returns null.

Description: Iterates over all entries in the collection, applying a given operation to each one.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Reads from a concurrent hash set.
Technique 2: Acquires a read lock on a shared resource.

Description: This method removes a specific listener from a collection of registered listeners. It ensures thread-safe access to the listener collection during the removal process and then notifies the removed listener that it has been unregistered.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method is part of a default interface method and serves as a placeholder. It does not perform any action when called.

This operation is performed to maintain a record of the last activity, particularly in scenarios where the system might be shutting down.

Description: This method formats an informational message that includes a provided string, the absolute path to a lock file, and optionally an exception's message. It then logs this formatted message at the INFO level if logging is enabled.

Description: This method defines the type of lock to be used, which is primarily relevant when the lock annotation is not directly applied to a collection or document parameter or return type.

Description: This method logs information about a lock event, including the event type, group ID, entry ID, lock details, owner, count, timestamp, and the first stack trace if available. It performs this logging only if the specified log level is enabled.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method acquires a read lock on a specified collection and all its descendant collections. This ensures that the data within the collection cannot be modified while the lock is held.

Return value description: A LockGroup object containing the identifier for the lock group and an array of LockedPath objects representing the locks acquired on each segment of the path.

Description: This method acquires a read lock for a specified B-tree file to ensure exclusive access during read operations and returns a managed lock object that includes the lock and a mechanism for releasing it.

Technique 2: Internal tracking of lock attempts and acquisitions via LockTable

Description: This method attempts to acquire a write lock on a specific B-tree file, ensuring exclusive access for modifications.

Technique 3: Exception handling for lock acquisition failures

Description: This method specifies the mode for a held lock, with a default of no lock. It allows for an alternative mode parameter to be used if the primary mode is not specified. Return value description: The lock mode. It can be one of the predefined Lock.LockMode values, defaulting to Lock.LockMode.NO_LOCK.

Description: This method defines the type of lock to be used.
Return value description: Returns the type of lock, defaulting to UNKNOWN if not specified.

Technique 2: Updates a LockTable to reflect a released lock.

Description: Creates a document lock that indicates a document is not currently locked.

Technique 2: XML stream writing to format data as XML.
Technique 3: Logging errors using a logging framework.

It also includes the hold count and any associated stack traces.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method attempts to save a file lock. If the lock is not available, it throws an exception and unschedules the firing trigger.

Checks if a given document identifier exists within the system's internal mapping.
