Description: Registers a listener to receive notifications about journal events.
This method is invoked after a journal checkpoint has been successfully written, and it receives the identifier of the transaction that was part of the checkpoint.
Return value description: A boolean value indicating whether this listener should continue to be notified of future events or be removed from the notification list.

Description: This method constructs a new Lsn object using the provided byte array and offset.
Return value description: A new Lsn object representing a log sequence number.

Description: This method reads raw byte data from a buffer and constructs a logical sequence number (LSN) object.
Return value description: An Lsn object representing a logical sequence number.

Description: Copies raw data from an internal buffer to a provided byte array.
Appends the current log sequence number (LSN) to the provided byte buffer.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method compares two LSN (Log Sequence Number) objects to determine their order. It handles cases where one or both LSNs are considered invalid, treating invalid LSNs as smaller than valid ones. For valid LSNs, it performs a lexicographical comparison of their underlying integer arrays.
Return value description: Returns an integer indicating the comparison result: negative if the current LSN is less than the other LSN, positive if it is greater, and zero if they are equal.

Description: This method writes the current entry's data into the provided byte buffer.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: Reads data from a buffer to reconstruct an entry.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method redoes an underlying operation as part of a recovery process, potentially throwing an exception if the operation cannot be completed.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This operation reverses or rolls back a previous underlying action, typically as part of a recovery process.
Return value description: This method does not return a value, but it may throw a LogException if the rollback fails.

Description: This method provides a human-readable summary of the entry's state for debugging.
Return value description: A string containing a detailed description of the entry, useful for troubleshooting.

Description: Registers a new type of loggable entry, associating a byte identifier with a function that can construct a specific loggable object.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method creates a loggable object based on a given type, using a provided broker and transaction ID. If no loggable is defined for the specified type, it returns null. An exception is thrown if the loggable cannot be created.
Return value description: A loggable object corresponding to the requested type, or null if no loggable is defined for that type.
Technique 2: In-memory map lookup for type association

Description: This method updates the transaction identifier for subsequent operations within the journal log.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method represents an action that can be undone and redone, but in this specific implementation, it performs no operation when asked to redo.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method is designed to perform an undo operation, but currently, it has no implementation and therefore does nothing.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method generates a string representation of a log entry, including its logical sequence number (LSN) and the class name of the object it represents.
Return value description: A string formatted as '[LSN] ClassName '.

Description: This method retrieves the subsequent log entry from the current position within the journal. It checks if the end of the journal has been reached before attempting to read the entry.
Return value description: The next loggable entry from the journal, or null if no more entries are available. A LogException is thrown if there's an issue reading the journal.
Technique 1: File system access to read journal metadata.
Technique 2: In-memory data structure manipulation for position tracking.

Description: This method retrieves the immediately preceding log entry. It handles cases where there is no prior entry and throws an exception if disk inconsistencies prevent reading.
Return value description: The previous log entry if one exists, otherwise null.

Description: This method retrieves the most recent log entry from the journal.
Return value description: It returns the last log entry, or null if the journal is empty. It may throw a LogException if there is an issue reading the journal due to disk inconsistencies.

Description: This method repositions the file pointer to the beginning of a log entry identified by a given Log Sequence Number (LSN). This operation is crucial for reading or processing specific parts of a log file sequentially.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method resets the file pointer to the beginning of the journal, skipping over the header, to prepare for reading the first entry.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method repositions the file pointer to the end of the journal file, preparing it for appending new entries.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method releases resources held by a file channel. It closes the file channel if it is open and then nullifies the reference to it, logging any errors that occur during the closing process.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method attempts to acquire a lock on the journal log directory to prevent concurrent access by other eXist processes. If the directory is already locked, it throws an exception indicating the conflict and the last access time of the lock file.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method writes a journal entry to a log, preparing it with necessary metadata such as transaction ID, size, and checksum. It ensures the entry fits within buffer limits and manages transaction tracking. If the buffer is full, it flushes the existing content before writing the new entry.
This method retrieves the most recently recorded LSN (Log Sequence Number) that has been physically written to the journal.
Return value description: The last LSN that was physically written to the journal.

Description: This method writes the buffered data to disk, optionally forcing all changes to be persisted to the storage medium.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method writes buffered data to disk, optionally ensuring all changes are permanently stored by forcing a file system synchronization. It also checks if the journal size has exceeded a limit, and if so, triggers a checkpoint operation.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: File I/O for buffer flushing and synchronization.
Technique 2: Logging for error and warning messages.

Description: This method writes a checkpoint record to a journal and optionally starts a new journal file if the current one is too large. It handles file switching and asynchronously removes the old journal file. The operation is synchronized to ensure data integrity.
Technique 2: Managing file operations, including switching and removal.
Technique 3: Asynchronous file deletion using a separate thread.

Description: This method switches to a new journal file with a higher file number. If a file already exists at the target location, it is first renamed with a '.bak' extension. The current journal file is closed, and a new one is created and initialized.
Technique 1: File system operations (checking existence, moving, creating, writing)

Description: Writes a journal header to a byte channel, including a magic number and the journal format version.
Return value description: None.

Description: This method ensures that all buffered data is written to disk and then closes the underlying file channel, logging any errors that occur during the synchronization process.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method extracts a journal file number from a given file path. It parses the base name of the file, assuming it's a hexadecimal representation of the file number, and validates that this number is within a valid range.
Return value description: A short integer representing the journal file number extracted from the file name.

Description: This method determines the highest numbered journal file from a provided stream of file paths. It is used to identify the most recent journal file for operations such as recovery or logging.
Return value description: Returns the number of the last journal file found, or -1 if the input stream of files was empty.

Description: This method shuts down the journal. It optionally writes a checkpoint record to the log to ensure a clean closure for recovery purposes. It then flushes any pending data, closes the underlying channel, and releases any file locks.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Logging calls are made to record the shutdown process and any errors.

Description: This method cleans up resources by closing a channel and deleting a file, logging any errors encountered during the process.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method initiates the shutdown of the resource pool without waiting for ongoing tasks to complete.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method creates a new B-tree index, populates it with a specified number of key-value pairs, and then prints the contents of the B-tree to standard output. Before creating the new index, it first deletes any existing file associated with the index.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Database Call: Creates and manipulates a B-tree index, implying interaction with a database storage mechanism.
Technique 2: File Operation: Deletes an existing file and creates a new file for the B-tree index.
Technique 3: Output Operation: Writes the contents of the B-tree to standard output.

Description: This method rebuilds a B-tree data structure, opens it, performs the rebuild operation, prints its contents to standard output, and then closes it.
Technique 1: Database calls are made to interact with the B-tree structure.
Technique 2: File I/O operations are performed for reading and writing to the B-tree file.

Description: This method reads a specified number of keys from a B-tree data structure. For each key, it attempts to find its corresponding value within the B-tree. If a key is not found, it prints a message indicating so.
Return value description: This method does not return any value. Its purpose is to perform an action (reading from a B-tree) and potentially print messages to the console.

Description: This program performs operations on a B-tree data structure based on command-line arguments. It can create a B-tree of a specified size, rebuild it, or read data from it. The program handles potential database, termination, and I/O exceptions, and ensures the B-tree is shut down afterward.
Return value description: The method returns void as it is the main entry point of the program and its actions are executed via side effects.

Description: This method displays a document's content, checks if it's locked by another user, prompts the current user to proceed if locked, and then attempts to acquire a lock for the current user to allow editing. If an error occurs during locking, the document is made read-only. Finally, the document view is made visible.
Return value description: This method returns void.
Technique 1: Makes a database call to retrieve user account information and check for resource locks.
Technique 2: Makes a database call to lock the resource for the current user.
Technique 3: Displays a confirmation dialog to the user.

Description: This method updates a progress bar to reflect the current status of a process. It sets the progress bar to a specific value and displays a text message indicating whether elements or nodes are being stored.
This method determines if a given file or directory should be accepted based on whether it ends with the .zip extension or if it is a directory.
Return value description: Returns true if the file is a directory or has a .zip extension, otherwise returns false.

Description: This method executes a given client action and, if an exception occurs during its execution, it invokes a specified failure action with the exception details.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method executes a predefined action that is critical for the system's operation. It is designed to throw an exception if any part of the action processing encounters an error.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: Compares this favorite to another object based on their connection names.
Return value description: Returns a negative integer, zero, or a positive integer as this favorite's connection name is lexicographically less than, equal to, or greater than the other object's string representation.

Description: This method finalizes an operation by accepting a response object. It signals the completion of a task, making the result available.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method removes a specified Range Index from a collection of indices. It ensures the index to be deleted exists within the current set of indices before proceeding with the removal.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Array manipulation for removal of an element.

Description: This method updates the details of a specific range index, identified by its numeric index. It can modify the index's type, its XPath expression, or its XML Schema type based on the provided parameters. If a parameter is null, the corresponding detail of the index remains unchanged.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Modifies an in-memory data structure representing range indexes.

Description: This method adds a new range index configuration, specifying the type of index (path or qualified name), the XPath expression to index, and the corresponding XML Schema type.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method removes a trigger from a list of triggers based on its numerical index. If the trigger to be removed is the last one, the entire list is cleared. Otherwise, a new list is created excluding the specified trigger.
Return value description: None. This method modifies the internal state of the object.

Description: This method updates the class and parameters for a specific trigger within a collection's configuration. It marks the configuration as changed and conditionally updates the trigger's class if a new class name is provided.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method adds a new trigger to a list of triggers, initializing the list if it doesn't exist or expanding it if it does. The method marks that a change has occurred.
This method checks if the collection's configuration has been modified.
Return value description: Returns true if the configuration has changed, and false otherwise.

Description: This method saves the current collection configuration to a file named 'collection.xconf' within the specified collection. It will create the collection and the configuration file if they do not already exist.
Return value description: The method returns 'true' if the configuration was saved successfully, and 'false' if any errors occurred during the process.
Technique 1: Database call to create a collection.
Technique 2: Database call to create a resource.
Technique 3: Database call to store a resource.

Description: Generates an XML representation of a range index configuration, including its path or qualified name, and the index type.
Return value description: A string containing the XML configuration for the range index.
Technique 1: String manipulation using StringBuilder for efficient string construction.

Description: This method generates an XML string representing a trigger, including its class name and any associated parameters.
Return value description: An XML formatted string representing the trigger configuration.

Description: This method processes command-line arguments to configure various client options and operations.
Return value description: Returns a CommandlineOptions object containing the parsed and processed command-line arguments.

Description: This method attempts to terminate an active XQuery execution if one is running, and then clears the reference to the active execution context.
Technique 1: Accessing and modifying shared mutable state
Technique 2: Interacting with an XQuery execution engine

Description: This method processes an XQuery, displays its compiled structure and results, and updates the user interface with progress and status messages. It handles potential errors during query execution and resource retrieval, and finally logs the executed query to the history.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: Retrieves a collection of XML documents from the database, starting from the root. If an error occurs during retrieval, an error message is displayed to the user.
Return value description: The method returns null as it is designed for its side effects.
Technique 1: Database call to retrieve a collection of XML documents.
Technique 2: Error handling to display messages to the user.

Description: This method manages a list of collection names, first checking if a loading indicator is present at the end of the list and removing it if found. Then, it adds a new set of collection names to the list.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 2: Checks for a specific item in a list.
Technique 3: Removes an item from a list.

Description: This method simulates a click action on a button when the Enter key is pressed. It checks if the source of the key event is an AbstractButton or a text input field (JPasswordField, JTextField, JComboBox). If the Enter key is pressed on an AbstractButton, it directly triggers a click. If pressed on a text input field, it triggers a click on a designated button. This behavior is commonly used to improve user experience by allowing activation of controls with the keyboard.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method renders an icon, and if the icon's selection state is indeterminate, it draws a filled rectangle and an outline within the icon's bounds. The color of the rectangle and outline changes based on whether the component is enabled.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method handles user interaction with a tristate checkbox. When the checkbox is in a deselected state, it is set to a false selected state. Otherwise, it updates the checkbox's selection state to the next state in its cycle (selected, indeterminate, or deselected) and stores this state internally.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method provides a default state for a tristate checkbox, indicating that its state is currently undetermined.
Return value description: Returns the INDETERMINATE state, signifying an undefined or mixed state.

Description: This method returns a predefined state indicating that an item is selected.
Return value description: Returns the 'SELECTED' state from the TristateState enum, signifying a selected item.

Description: This method is part of a state machine, and in this particular state, it always transitions to the 'DESELECTED' state. It represents a fixed transition that doesn't depend on any input or internal logic beyond its current state.
Return value description: Returns the 'DESELECTED' state, indicating a specific state within a tristate system.

Description: This method advances the state of a tristate checkbox to its next logical state.
Return value description: The method returns the new state of the tristate checkbox.

Description: This method converts a nullable Boolean value into a TristateState. If the input Boolean is null, it returns an INDETERMINATE state. If the input Boolean is true, it returns a SELECTED state. If the input Boolean is false, it returns a DESELECTED state.
Return value description: A TristateState representing the converted Boolean value.

Description: This method converts a tristate state into a standard boolean value. It maps 'DESELECTED' to false and 'SELECTED' to true, while other states result in a null value.
Return value description: A Boolean object representing the converted state, or null if the input state is not 'DESELECTED' or 'SELECTED'.

Description: This method registers a callback to be executed when a dialog completes and provides a string response.
Return value description: void

Description: This method checks if the text content of a JTextField component matches a predefined pattern. If the input component is not a JTextField, it returns false.
Return value description: Returns true if the text in the JTextField matches the pattern, and false otherwise.

Description: This method enables auto-completion functionality for a given JComboBox by making it editable and setting up an AutoCompletion listener.
Return value description: Returns an AutoCompletion object that manages the auto-completion behavior for the provided JComboBox.
Technique 2: Instantiates and returns a new object

Description: This method configures a text editor component, attaching and detaching event listeners for key presses and focus changes, and setting the document for the editor.
Return value description: None.

Description: This method handles the removal of text within a document, specifically within the context of a combo box. It adjusts the selection and cursor position based on whether the backspace key was pressed, or delegates to the superclass for standard text removal. It also includes logic to prevent modification while an item is being selected and provides auditory feedback when attempting to delete at the beginning of the document.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 2: Utilizes Swing event handling for user input (backspace).
Technique 3: Performs document manipulation within a PlainDocument.

Description: This method inserts text into a document, attempts to find a matching item based on the current text, and then updates the selection in a combo box. If no match is found, it provides audible feedback and maintains the previously selected item.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 2: Interaction with a combo box for item selection and display
Technique 3: Playing an audible beep for user feedback

Description: This method takes a string as input and returns it as an object. It's a simple identity function for strings, ensuring that the input string is treated as an object.
Return value description: The returned value is the original string that was passed into the method, now cast to an Object.

Description: This method converts an object to its string representation. It is specifically designed to handle string inputs.
Return value description: The method returns the input object cast directly to a String. If the input object is not a String, a ClassCastException will occur.

Description: This method creates a new user account. It first determines the user's primary group, then creates a personal group for the user if selected. It then configures the user's details, assigns them to groups, sets their primary group, and finally adds the user account to the system. If a personal group was created, the user is also designated as its manager.
Technique 1: Database call to add user account

Description: This method converts a string representing an octal number (umask) into its integer equivalent.
Return value description: An integer representing the octal umask.

Description: This method converts an integer representation of a file permission mask into its octal string equivalent, ensuring it is zero-padded to four digits.
Return value description: An octal string representing the input integer, formatted to be four digits long with leading zeros if necessary.

Description: This method is intended to register the current object as a manager within the system. However, the current implementation is empty and does not perform any actions.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method is intended to create a group, but instead, it immediately calls a method to update an existing group.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method checks if the current user has the necessary permissions to modify the members of a specific group. It verifies if the user is a database administrator or if they are listed as a manager for the group.
Technique 3: Displays an error message to the user.

Description: This method determines if a selected group member can be modified based on whether a group member is selected and if the selected member is a restricted user within specific groups. It prevents modification of critical system users like the DBA or GUEST user.
Return value description: Returns a boolean value indicating whether the selected group member can be modified.
Technique 1: Checks the selection state of a JTable to determine if a row is selected.
Technique 2: Performs string comparisons to check user and group names against predefined system constants.

Description: This method refreshes the displayed list of users in a table. It clears the existing entries and then populates the table with current user account information, sorted by name. If an error occurs while fetching the user list, an error message is displayed to the user.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Retrieves user data from a user management service.
Technique 2: Displays error messages to the user via a dialog box.
Technique 3: Updates a table model with new data.

Description: This method refreshes the displayed list of user groups in a table. It clears the existing table data and then populates it with an updated list of group names and their descriptions retrieved from a user management service. If an error occurs during data retrieval, an error message is shown to the user.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Database call to retrieve group information.
Technique 2: Retrieval of group descriptions from a user management service.
Technique 3: Displaying error messages to the user via a dialog box.

Description: This method handles the creation or update of a user. It first checks if the user is assigned to at least one group. If not, it displays an error message. Otherwise, it proceeds to update the user and then notifies any registered callbacks with the updated password if it has been changed.
Return value description: This method does not explicitly return a value, but it may trigger callbacks with the updated password if it has changed.
Technique 1: Displays a message dialog to the user.
Technique 2: Iterates through a list of callbacks to notify them of an event.

Description: Registers a callback to be executed when a dialog completes with a string response. This allows the system to react to user input or dialog outcomes by invoking the provided callback function.
This method registers a callback to be executed when a dialog completes and provides a response. It adds the provided callback to a collection of existing dialog completion callbacks.
Return value description: void

Description: This method adds a new element to a list model. If the element is successfully added, it signals that the contents of the list have changed.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.
Technique 2: Triggers an event to notify listeners about data changes.

Description: This method adds a collection of elements to a sorted list model and then notifies any listeners of the change.
This method clears the entire contents of the data model and notifies listeners that the data has changed.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method checks if a given element exists within the collection.
Return value description: Returns true if the element is found in the collection, and false otherwise.

Description: This method retrieves the first element from a collection of items.
Return value description: The first element of the collection.

Description: This method provides an iterator for traversing the elements within the model. It acts as an entry point to access the collection of items sequentially.
Return value description: An iterator that allows for sequential access to the elements contained within the model.

Description: This method returns the last element from a model.
Return value description: The last element of type T from the model.

Description: This method attempts to remove a specific element from the model. If the element is successfully removed, it notifies any listeners about the change.
This method translates a permission object into a displayable mode object, extracting read, write, and execute permissions for the owner, group, and others, as well as sticky and setuid/setgid bits.
Return value description: A ModeDisplay object representing the parsed permission details.

Description: This method modifies the permission settings of a given Permission object based on a set of boolean flags representing read, write, and execute permissions for owner, group, and others, as well as set UID, set GID, and sticky bits. It only updates permissions that are explicitly defined (not indeterminate).
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Bitwise operations for modifying permission flags
Technique 2: Conditional logic for applying specific permissions

Description: This method removes a specified portion of text from a document, but only if the resulting text, after removal, adheres to a defined mask.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method intercepts string insertions into a document, validating the insertion against a umask before allowing it to proceed.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method modifies the content of a document by removing a specified portion and inserting new text at a given offset. It performs validation to ensure the resulting content adheres to a Umask constraint before applying the changes. If the validation fails, the original document content is preserved.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 3: Validating input against a defined constraint

Description: This method adds the current user to the group members table, designating them as a manager.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.
Technique 1: Adds a row to a table model.

Description: This method creates a new group, adds users to it, and designates managers for the group based on user input from a form. It handles potential errors during group and user management operations by displaying error messages and stopping the process. Finally, it closes the current dialog window.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Database calls to manage groups and users.
Technique 2: UI interactions for displaying error messages.

Description: This method determines if the current user has permission to modify group members.
Return value description: Returns true if the user can modify group members, and false otherwise.

Description: Checks if a row in the group members table has been selected, indicating whether a group member can be modified.
Return value description: Returns true if a row is selected in the group members table, and false otherwise.

Description: This method registers a callback function that will be invoked when a dialog completes and provides a string response.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method determines if a given file should be accepted based on whether it is a directory or has a valid file extension. It allows directories to be viewed and filters files by checking if their extension is present in a predefined list.
Return value description: Returns true if the file is a directory or has an allowed extension, and false otherwise.

Description: This method creates a new LabelledBoolean object with the same label as the current object, but with a potentially new boolean value.
Return value description: A new LabelledBoolean object.

Description: Registers a callback to be executed upon the completion of a dialog that returns a response.
This method displays a comprehensive list of available commands and their descriptions to the user, categorized into general, search, and user management operations.
Return value description: This method does not return any value; its purpose is to print information to the console.

Description: This method serves as the entry point for the interactive client application. It validates the Java version, parses command-line arguments, initializes the interactive client, and then executes its main run loop. It handles various exceptions related to startup, arguments, and general errors, exiting with appropriate status codes.
Technique 2: Exception handling for application startup and execution

Description: This method is responsible for creating and initializing a new thread for a client instance, allowing for concurrent operations.
Return value description: Returns a newly created Thread object that is ready to be started and executed.

Description: This method establishes a connection to an XML database, initializing and configuring the database instance, and then retrieves the root collection for subsequent operations. It handles driver registration, property settings for SSL and configuration, and user authentication.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method reloads the XML database collection and retrieves its resources. It establishes a connection to the XML database using provided properties and then fetches all associated resources.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 2: Internal method call to get resources

Description: This method displays a given string on the console, paginated into 24-line segments. It prompts the user to press Enter to continue or 'q' to quit after each segment.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Reading from standard input to control pagination.
Technique 2: Writing to standard output for displaying document content and prompts.
Technique 3: Reading from a string as if it were a file.

Description: This method processes a user-entered command line, executing various operations against an eXist-db database. It handles commands for managing collections, resources, users, and executing queries. If a GUI is active, it updates the UI accordingly.
Technique 1: Database calls are made to interact with the eXist-db. This includes operations like retrieving collections, resources, user accounts, and executing queries.
Technique 2: File system operations are performed for reading command files and processing local files for upload.
Technique 3: String parsing is used to interpret user commands and their arguments.

Description: This method retrieves a resource based on its URI, using a configured indentation property.
Return value description: A Resource object representing the retrieved data.

Description: This method retrieves a resource from a collection based on a provided URI. If the resource is not found, it logs a message and returns null.
Return value description: A resource object if found, otherwise null.
Technique 1: Database call (implied by XmldbURI and Resource types)

Description: This method stores a given file or all files within a directory. It handles both individual files and directories, recursively processing subdirectories if configured. The method determines the MIME type of each file and then stores it in a resource collection, optionally providing verbose progress updates.
Return value description: Returns TRUE if all files within the specified directory or the individual file were successfully stored; otherwise, it may indicate failure through exceptions.

Description: This method processes specified files or directories, identifying compressed files (ending in .gz or .Z) and their mime types, and then stores them as resources within a collection. It can recursively process directories if configured to do so and handles both readable files and files found via a directory scanner.
Return value description: The method returns true if the operation succeeded.

Description: This method stores the contents of a zip file into a database, creating necessary directories as it goes. It also handles potential security threats by checking for archive exit attacks.
Return value description: Returns true if the operation of storing the zip file's contents was successful.

Description: This method processes a list of selected files for upload. It makes the upload dialog visible, sets the total size of the files to be uploaded, and then iteratively stores each file. The process can be cancelled by the user during iteration. Finally, it signals that the upload is complete.

This method orchestrates the initialization and execution of an interactive client application. It sets up the client's environment, including configuration, connection to a database, and the user interface (command-line or graphical).
Return value description: Returns true if the client application successfully initialized and processed its actions, and false if an error occurred during initialization or processing.

Description: This method initializes the graphical user interface (GUI) for the client application. Description: This method is responsible for exiting a service mode, potentially signaling the system to revert to a standard operational state. It may involve state changes and resource cleanup.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method logs a message indicating the start of a zip creation process for restore data, including the total uncompressed size of the data in a human-readable format.
This method serves as a placeholder and does not perform any action when a file is added to a zip archive for transfer.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: Logs a message indicating that the zip file containing restore data has been successfully created and is ready for transfer.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: Logs a message indicating that the restore data transfer to the remote server has started, including the human-readable size of the transfer.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method does nothing.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method logs a message indicating that the transfer of restore data to a remote server has been completed.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method initiates the backup restoration process, logging a message to indicate the start of the operation.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method initiates a restore process using a provided backup descriptor.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method logs information about the creation of a specified collection.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method logs a message indicating that a specified resource has been restored. It is used to provide visibility into the state changes of resources within the system.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method logs a warning message indicating that a specified number of resources are being skipped, along with an accompanying message providing more context.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: Logs a message indicating that the backup restore process has completed.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method processes a collection using a database broker and a transaction, handling potential exceptions related to permissions, locks, and syntax errors by re-throwing them as XMLDB exceptions.
Return value description: Returns a result of type R, which is the outcome of the underlying processing or an error indicator if an exception occurs.
Technique 1: Database call (implied by DBBroker and Txn)
Technique 2: Exception handling for various error conditions

Description: This method applies a function to a database collection, which may involve database operations and potentially trigger exceptions related to permissions, locking, syntax, or IO.
This method applies an operation to a database broker within a transaction, handling potential permission, I/O, or vendor-specific errors by re-throwing them as XMLDB exceptions.
Return value description: Returns the result of the underlying operation applied to the database broker and transaction.

Description: This method applies a given function to an XML database (XMLDB) using a provided broker and transaction, returning the result of that function. It handles various potential exceptions including database, permission, I/O, XPath, and general XMLDB errors.
Return value description: The result of the applied function, which is expected to be of a type determined by the function itself.

Description: This method applies an operation to an XML document, handling potential exceptions related to permissions, locks, and syntax errors by re-throwing them as XMLDB exceptions.
Return value description: The method returns a result of type R, which is the outcome of the applied operation.

Description: This method applies a function to a document within a database transaction, utilizing a database broker. It handles potential errors related to XML database operations, permissions, locking, I/O, and syntax.
Return value description: The result of applying the function to the document.

Description: This method processes a given XMLDB URI, potentially reformatting it to remove user information if an XMLDB prefix is present. It ensures the URI has a valid scheme and then delegates further processing to a superclass method.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method parses a given URI path to determine the API type (local, XML-RPC, WebDAV, or REST) and extracts relevant path segments for context and further processing. It handles different URI structures, including those with or without explicit port numbers and common API suffixes. The method also ensures that local URIs do not specify a port, throwing an exception if they do. It then delegates the remaining path processing to its superclass.
Return value description: This method does not return any value, but it modifies the state of the object by setting `apiName` and `context` based on the parsed path.
Technique 2: Conditional logic for API type determination

Description: This method reconstructs and updates a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) based on various components like instance name, host, port, context, and collection path. It ensures that the URI remains valid and reverts to the previous URI if an error occurs during reconstruction.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method normalizes the current context, which is an XML database URI, by applying standard URI normalization rules and updating the context part of the XML database URI.
Return value description: It returns a normalized XML database URI, or the original URI if no context is currently set.

Description: This method determines a relative URI based on a given URI and the system's current context.
Return value description: A URI representing the provided URI relative to the current context.
Technique 1: Logging information about the current context.
Technique 2: Creating new URI objects from strings.

Description: This method constructs a fully qualified URI by combining a base context URI with a relative URI string. It ensures the context URI has a trailing slash before resolving the relative URI against it.
Return value description: A resolved URI object that represents the combination of the base context and the provided relative URI string.

Description: This method resolves a given URI against a configured context, ensuring the context URI has a trailing slash before performing the resolution. It validates that both the input URI and the internal context are not null.
Return value description: The method returns a new URI that is the result of resolving the input URI against the configured context URI.

Description: This method verifies if a given account is the owner of a specified collection.
Return value description: Returns true if the account matches the collection's owner, and false otherwise.

Description: This method verifies if a given user has the specified permission level for a collection.
Return value description: Returns true if the user has the required permissions, false otherwise.

Description: This method ensures that all pending data is written to disk by synchronizing the database. It checks if a synchronization is needed before proceeding with the operation.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method generates a unique name for a database resource, ensuring it doesn't conflict with existing documents or collections within the eXist instance. The name is formed by a hexadecimal representation of a random integer, suffixed with '.xml'.
Return value description: A unique string representing the name of a database resource, formatted as 'xxxxxxxx.xml'.
Technique 1: Database call to check for document existence.
Technique 2: Database call to check for child collection existence.

Description: This method creates a new resource, either an XMLResource or a BinaryResource, based on the provided type and ID. If an ID is not provided, a new one is generated. It handles potential URI syntax errors and unknown resource types.
Return value description: A newly created resource instance of the specified type (either XMLResource or BinaryResource).

Description: This method checks if a specific service type is available within the system's service provider cache.
Retrieves a specific service implementation based on its class type from a cached collection of service providers.
Return value description: An optional containing the requested service implementation if found, otherwise an empty optional.

Description: This method registers various service implementations with a provider registry. It configures local implementations for query services (XPath, XQuery, XUpdate), collection management, user management, database instance management, index queries, and restoration services.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.
Technique 1: Dependency Injection: Services are instantiated and provided with their dependencies (user, brokerPool, this).
Technique 2: Service Registration: Implemented services are registered against their respective interface types within a registry.

Description: This method retrieves a list of the names of all direct child collections within the current collection.
Return value description: A list of strings, where each string is the name of a child collection.

Description: This method retrieves a list of resource URIs from a collection. It iterates through the documents in the collection, acquires a read lock for each document, and adds its URI to the list if it's not a null resource.
Return value description: A list of strings, where each string is the file URI of a resource within the collection.

Description: This method removes a resource from the database, handling both XML and binary types. It first verifies the existence of the resource and then proceeds with its deletion based on its type. The operation is performed within a transaction and utilizes locking mechanisms to ensure data integrity.
This method stores a resource, delegating to another method with additional parameters that are not provided.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method stores a resource, determining whether to store it as an XML or binary resource based on its type. It also updates the resource's creation and modification dates, marks it as not new, and flags the system for synchronization.
Technique 2: Database call (implied by `XMLDBException` and `storeXMLResource`/`storeBinaryResource` which are likely database interactions)

Description: This method provides a way to safely execute read-only operations against an XML database collection. It ensures that the operations do not modify the data and uses the database user credentials configured for the collection. The returned function encapsulates these read-only operations, allowing them to be applied to the collection.
Return value description: A function that accepts a read-only operation to be performed against the collection and returns the result of that operation, potentially throwing an XMLDBException.

Description: This method provides a way to perform operations on a database collection under a specified lock mode, using a given transaction and broker. It returns a function that accepts an operation to be executed on the locked collection.
Return value description: A function that takes an operation to be performed on the locked database collection and returns the result of that operation.

Description: This method is called when a zip file transfer is initiated and records the total uncompressed size of the data being transferred.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: Records that a file has been added to a zip archive for transfer, along with its uncompressed size.
This method signals the completion of a zip file creation process intended for transfer.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method records that a transfer has started and keeps track of the total size of the transfer.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method facilitates the transfer of data in defined chunks.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method signifies the completion of a data transfer operation.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method is called when the system starts and receives the total number of files that need to be processed.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method processes a backup descriptor string.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method creates a new collection at the specified URI.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method restores a resource identified by its Uniform Resource Identifier (URI).
This method processes a message by skipping a specified number of resources.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method logs an informational message to the console. It is used for providing feedback or status updates during program execution.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method logs a warning message. It is used to indicate potential issues or non-critical errors that do not prevent the program from continuing its execution.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method logs an error message.
This method signals the completion of a process or task. It doesn't return any data and does not interact with external systems.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method determines the full path of a collection based on a given name, either by resolving it against an existing collection's path or by returning the name as is if no existing collection is present.
Return value description: The method returns an XmldbURI representing the resolved or original collection path.

Description: This method processes an input parameter to extract ACEAider objects, returning an empty stream if the input is null or not an array.
Return value description: A stream of ACEAider objects.

Description: This method executes a given query against an XML database and returns the results.
Return value description: The results of the executed query, formatted as a ResourceSet.

Description: This method processes an XPath query against an XML resource obtained from a previous query, returning the results of that query.
Return value description: The results of executing the provided XPath query against the input XML resource.

Description: This method takes an XQuery string and returns a representation of the query that is ready to be executed.
Return value description: A compiled representation of the XQuery, which can be used to execute the query multiple times.

Description: This method attempts to compile an XQuery expression, checking for any static errors during the process. If the compilation is successful, it returns an object representing the compiled query.
Return value description: A compiled representation of the XQuery, which can be used to execute the query later.
Technique 2: Error checking for static XQuery errors

Description: This method executes a query against a data source and returns the results. It handles potential errors during query execution.
Return value description: The results of the executed query, returned as a ResourceSet.

Description: This method executes a pre-compiled XQuery, ensuring that all declared namespaces and variables are passed to the query for execution.
Return value description: The results of the executed XQuery are returned as a ResourceSet.

Description: Executes a compiled XQuery expression using the results of a previous query, passing along any declared namespaces and variables.
Return value description: Returns a set of resources that represent the results of the executed query.

Description: This method removes a namespace mapping from an internal map, optionally targeting the default namespace if the provided prefix is null or empty. It may encounter errors specific to the underlying vendor implementation.

This method declares a global, external XQuery variable and assigns it an initial value. Any Java object can be passed as the initial value, and the implementation will attempt to map it to a corresponding XQuery value, including basic Java types, arrays, DOM node types, and XMLResources.
Return value description: This method returns void.

Description: This operation removes any previously defined variables within the system.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method generates a diagnostic dump of a previously executed query and writes it to a provided writer.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: Initiates a data restore operation from a specified backup path. It handles different backup formats (zip files or directories), uploads the backup, and then starts the restore process remotely. The method monitors the progress of the restore task by polling for events and notifies a listener about the restore's status, including started, processing, resource restoration, skipped resources, informational messages, warnings, errors, and completion. It also manages the administrator password, updating it if a new one is provided during the restore process.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: File system operations (checking existence, reading, writing, zipping, deleting)
Technique 2: Remote procedure calls (RPC) to execute restore and monitor task status

Description: This method initializes and returns a remote collection object, which represents a collection of XML documents stored remotely. It acts as a convenience method, calling another instance method with a null value for an additional parameter.
Return value description: A RemoteCollection object, representing a remote XML document collection.
Technique 1: Making a call to another internal method.

Description: This method checks if a remote collection exists and is accessible, then returns a representation of it if it is. If the collection does not exist or cannot be opened, it returns null.
Return value description: A RemoteCollection object representing the specified path if it exists and is accessible, otherwise null.
Technique 1: XML-RPC call to a remote server
Technique 2: Resource leasing for managing client connections

Description: This method executes a remote procedure call on an XML-RPC service. It first checks if the underlying client connection has been closed and throws an error if it has. Otherwise, it forwards the method name and parameters to the XML-RPC client for execution.
Return value description: The result of the remote procedure call, which can be any valid XML-RPC type.

Description: This method ensures that a lease associated with an XML-RPC client is properly closed, preventing errors if it has already been closed.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Conditional logic is used to check the state of the lease before attempting to close it.
Technique 2: An existing lease object is manipulated to close its associated resource.

Description: This method is responsible for creating a unique resource identifier by invoking an external service with the current path as a parameter.
Return value description: A string representing the newly created resource identifier.

Description: This method creates and returns a new resource of a specified type, identified by an ID. If no ID is provided, a new one is generated. It supports creating XML resources and binary resources.
Return value description: A new resource object of the requested type (e.g., XMLResource or BinaryResource) or an exception if the type is unsupported or the ID is invalid.
Technique 1: Database interaction (implied by XMLDBException and resource types)

Description: This method checks if a specific service type is available within the system's service provider cache.
Return value description: Returns true if the service type is found in the cache, and false otherwise.

Description: This method retrieves a specific service implementation from a cache based on its class type.
Return value description: An Optional containing the found service implementation if it exists, otherwise an empty Optional.

Description: This method registers various service implementations with a provider registry, enabling different interfaces to be resolved to their corresponding remote service proxies. It sets up mappings for query services, collection management, user management, database instance management, and restoration services.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: Checks if a child collection with the given name exists within the current collection.
Return value description: Returns true if a child collection with the specified name is found, false otherwise.
Technique 1: Iterating through a list of existing child collections.

Description: Retrieves a list of names for the child collections within the current collection.
Return value description: A list of strings, where each string is the name of a child collection.

Description: This method retrieves a list of available resources.
Return value description: A list of strings, where each string represents the name of a resource.

Description: This method removes a resource from the system, identified by its ID. It constructs the full URI for the resource and then executes a removal operation using that URI.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method stores a resource, delegating the storage operation to another method with additional parameters.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method stores a resource, either by uploading it directly or by saving it as a local file or stream. It handles different resource types and sizes, including binary and XML content, and sets creation and modification dates for remote resources.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.
Technique 1: File system access to check file readability and get file sizes.
Technique 2: Internal resource processing based on resource type and content.
Technique 3: Error handling for invalid resource operations.

Description: This method checks if a given Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) is valid for accessing the database, attempting to recover potentially malformed URIs before validation.
Return value description: Returns true if the provided URI is valid and accepted by the database, and false otherwise.

Description: This method determines if a given XMLDB URI is acceptable based on internal logic. It currently always returns true, indicating all URIs are accepted.

This method navigates to and retrieves a specific collection within a hierarchical database structure, given a URI path and an XML-RPC client for remote access. It handles the resolution of collection components and ensures the path exists.
Return value description: Returns a `Collection` object representing the specified collection in the database. If the collection is not found or the URI is invalid, an `XMLDBException` is thrown.

Description: This method executes a query against an XML database. It acts as a convenience method by calling an overloaded version of itself with a null value for an additional parameter.
Return value description: Returns a ResourceSet containing the results of the query.

Description: This method executes a query against a collection of XML data, optionally applying sorting, namespace mappings, and variable declarations. It then processes the results, handling any errors, and prepares them for return. If the query is successful and returns data, it also captures an identifier and hash for the results.
Return value description: The method returns a RemoteResourceSet containing the query results. This set includes the actual resources, a handle, and a hash if data was returned, along with properties inherited from the output configuration.

Description: This method compiles an XPath query string into an executable expression, handling potential compilation errors by re-throwing them as XMLDB exceptions.
Return value description: A compiled XPath expression ready for execution.

Description: This method compiles and validates an XQuery expression. It prepares optional parameters, including namespace mappings, variable declarations, and module load paths, before executing the compilation against a data collection. If an error occurs during compilation, it is thrown as an exception.
Return value description: The method returns a representation of the compiled XQuery expression, ready for execution.
Technique 1: Database call (to a collection's execute method)
Technique 2: HTTP call (implied by RpcAPI and remote execution)

Description: This method takes a source object, extracts its content as an XML query string, and then executes that query. It handles potential IO errors during content extraction by wrapping them in a custom exception.
Return value description: A ResourceSet containing the results of the executed query.

Description: This method executes a stored query against a collection, passing the provided Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) as a parameter. It handles potential errors returned by the query execution and constructs a resource set from the query results.
Return value description: A `ResourceSet` object representing the results of the stored query, including resources and associated metadata like an ID and hash.
Technique 1: Database call (to execute a stored query within the eXist-db collection)
Technique 2: RPC call (likely to interact with the eXist-db XML-RPC interface)

Description: This method executes an XML database query against a specified XML resource.
Return value description: A ResourceSet containing the results of the query.

Description: This method executes a query against an XML database, returning a set of resources that match the specified query criteria. It prepares parameters, including query details, sorting expressions, and collection-specific information, before sending them to the database for execution. If an error occurs during the query, it is caught and re-thrown.
Return value description: A RemoteResourceSet containing the query results, along with identifiers and hash values for managing the retrieved resources.

Description: This method retrieves a specific XML resource from a collection and then executes a query against it.
Return value description: Returns a ResourceSet containing the results of the query.

Description: This method clears all stored namespace mappings.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method removes a specified namespace from the system's namespace mappings. It ensures that the provided namespace string is no longer associated with any existing mapping.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method registers a new variable with an initial value within the system's scope.
This method removes all variable declarations currently stored.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method executes a compiled expression against a database and returns the resulting set of resources.
Return value description: A ResourceSet containing the results of the executed query.

Description: This method executes a compiled XML query against a specified XML resource, returning the results as a resource set. It acts as an entry point for processing existing compiled expressions.
Return value description: A ResourceSet containing the results of the executed query.

Description: This method prepares and executes a query against a remote XML database to retrieve diagnostic information, then writes the resulting string output to a provided writer. It handles optional parameters for namespaces and variable declarations, and sets a base URI for the query. The execution involves a database call to the 'printDiagnostics' function.
Return value description: This method does not return any value directly. It writes the diagnostic output to a provided `Writer` object.

Description: This method enables a protected mode for the system.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method disables a protected mode within the system.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method executes a provided function against a local eXist-db instance, leveraging a broker pool and user credentials to perform the database operation.
Return value description: The result of the database operation, which can be of any type R.

Description: This method executes a provided database operation within a managed transaction, ensuring atomicity and data consistency. It acquires a database broker from a pool, begins or continues a transaction, applies the user-defined operation, commits the transaction upon successful completion, and handles potential exceptions by re-throwing them as XMLDB exceptions.
This method executes a database operation within a transaction, leveraging an existing broker pool and user credentials.
Return value description: Returns the result of the provided database operation.

Description: This method executes a given database operation within a transaction, utilizing a local XML database connection pool, user credentials, and transactional context.
Return value description: It returns the result of the provided database operation.

Description: This method executes a given database operation within a transaction, leveraging an existing broker pool and user credentials.
Return value description: It returns the result of the database operation.

Description: This method creates or retrieves a collection within the database, optionally setting its creation timestamp. It then saves the collection's state and returns a local representation of it.
Return value description: A local representation of the created or retrieved collection, managed within a transaction.
Technique 1: Database call to get or create a collection.
Technique 2: Database call to save collection state.

Description: This method executes a provided database operation within a transaction context.
Return value description: The result of the database operation.

Description: This method executes a provided database operation within a transactional context, ensuring atomicity and consistency of database interactions.
Return value description: The result of the database operation.

Description: This method initiates the reindexing process for a collection of XML documents within a database by delegating to another method with the collection's path.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method reindexes a specified collection within the XML database. It is a deprecated method, with a newer alternative available.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method reindexes a specified collection within the XML database, ensuring its contents are efficiently searchable. It resolves the provided collection URI and then executes a 'reindexCollection' command with the collection path.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method reindexes a specific document within a collection. It constructs the full path to the document and then executes a reindexing operation on it. This process is typically used to update search indexes or other metadata associated with the document.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.
Technique 1: Database call: Executes a 'reindexDocument' command on the collection, implying an interaction with the underlying document store or database.
Technique 2: Path manipulation: Uses XmldbURI to construct and resolve document paths, indicating file or resource path handling.

Description: Configures a collection within the XML database using provided configuration data.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: Changes the owner group of the current collection to the specified group.
Return value description: None.

Description: Changes the owner of the current collection to the specified user account.
Return value description: None

Description: Changes the owner and group of the current collection.
Return value description: None

Description: This method changes the group ownership of a specified resource. It interacts with an underlying data store to update the resource's ownership information.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: Changes the owner of a specified resource to a given user.
Return value description: None.

Description: This method changes the owner and group of a specified resource. It interacts with security accounts and XML database resources.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method changes the access permissions for a specified resource based on a formatted string describing user, group, or other access levels and their associated read, write, or update privileges.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method changes the permissions for the current collection based on a string that describes the desired access rights.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method modifies the access permissions for a resource, potentially affecting who can read, write, or execute it.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method changes the access permissions for a given resource, potentially involving operations on a database and file system.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method is used to lock a specified resource for a given user, preventing other users from modifying it until the lock is released. Users with administrative privileges can bypass this lock.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: Determines if a given resource is locked by a user and, if so, returns the name of the user holding the lock. This method may interact with a database to check the lock status.
Return value description: Returns the name of the user who owns the lock on the resource, or null if the resource is not currently locked.

Description: This method releases a lock on a specified resource. It verifies that the user attempting to unlock the resource is either the one who locked it or an administrator.
Adds a new account to the system.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: Updates an existing account's information in the system.
This method updates the information for an existing group within the system. It handles potential errors during the update process by throwing an exception.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method adds a specified account to a specified group within an XML database.
This method adds a manager to a specified group within the XML database. It handles potential exceptions that may occur during the database operation.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method removes a specified manager from a given group within the XML database.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: Retrieves the permissions associated with all resources within the current collection. It returns these permissions in the order that the resources are listed.
Return value description: An array of Permission objects, corresponding to the permissions of each resource in the collection, in the same order as they are listed.

Description: This method retrieves the permissions associated with all direct child collections of the current collection.
Return value description: A list of `Permission` objects, where each object corresponds to the permissions of a child collection in the order they are listed.

Description: This method removes a user account from the system.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method removes a specified group from the system.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: Updates a user's group membership in the system, excluding password updates.
Return value description: None. The method's purpose is to perform an action (update user group) rather than return data.

Description: This method removes a specified account from a given group.
Return value description: None

Description: This method adds a new group to the system.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method adds a new user to the system. It is marked as deprecated and will be removed in version 1.6.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method updates an existing user's information. It is marked as deprecated and scheduled for removal after version 1.6.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method removes a user from the system. It is marked as deprecated and will be removed in a future version.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method locks a specified resource for a given user, preventing other users from accessing or modifying it. It is marked as deprecated and scheduled for removal in version 1.6.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method converts a standard URI to an XmldbURI. It serves as a public entry point for this conversion process.
Return value description: An XmldbURI object representing the converted standard URI.

Description: This method generates an XmldbURI object from a given string representation of an Xmldb URI. It acts as a convenience method for a more detailed URI construction process, defaulting to a specific behavior.
Return value description: An XmldbURI object representing the parsed and validated Xmldb URI.

Description: This method constructs an XmldbURI object from a given string representation of an XML:DB URI. It handles potential null input and can optionally escape characters within the URI string for proper formatting.
Return value description: An XmldbURI object representing the input XML:DB URI, or null if the input string was null.

Description: This method generates an XmldbURI object from a given string representation. It handles optional escaping of the URI string and enforces that the resulting URI must be an XMLDB URI if specified. It does not perform any database or HTTP calls.
Return value description: An XmldbURI object representing the parsed and validated XMLDB URI, or null if the input string was null.

Description: This method constructs an XmldbURI by combining an access URI with a collection path. It handles cases where the collection path might be null.
Return value description: An XmldbURI object representing the combined access and collection URIs, or null if the collection path is null.
