Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method is intended to save configuration but is explicitly designed to throw an exception, indicating that the effective user's configuration cannot be persisted.
Return value description: This method does not return a value as it always throws an exception.

Description: This method is designed to handle saving operations, but it explicitly disallows the persistence of the 'Effective User' by throwing an exception. This indicates that the Effective User's state is not intended to be stored directly.
Return value description: This method does not return a value as it always throws an UnsupportedOperationException.

Description: This method compares two Account objects based on their names, returning a negative integer, zero, or a positive integer as the first account's name is lexicographically less than, equal to, or greater than the second account's name.
Return value description: An integer indicating the lexicographical order of the account names.

Description: This method provides configuration values related to user settings and application modes. It utilizes default values if specific configurations are not provided.
Return value description: Returns the default configuration values for user settings and application modes.

Description: This method defines a default value for a byte group, which is set to an undefined state.
Return value description: The method returns a byte value representing the default state of the group.

Description: This method returns the current operating mode, which defaults to an undefined state if not explicitly set.
Return value description: The byte value representing the operating mode.

Description: This method determines and returns an enumeration value representing an ACE access type based on an integer input. If no matching ACE access type is found for the given integer, it throws an exception.
Return value description: An enumeration value of type ACE_ACCESS_TYPE that corresponds to the provided integer value.

Description: This method retrieves an ACE_TARGET enumeration value based on an integer input. If no matching value is found, it throws an exception indicating an unknown target.
Return value description: An ACE_TARGET enum value corresponding to the provided integer.

Description: This method adds an Access Control Entry (ACE) to a permission, specifying the type of access, the target of the access, and the name and mode of the permission. It may throw a PermissionDeniedException if the operation is not allowed.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: Adds an Access Control Entry (ACE) to a security policy, defining permissions for a specific target and access type, while also specifying a name and mode for the entry. This operation may fail if the caller does not have the necessary permissions to modify the security policy.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method adds an Access Control Entry (ACE) to a permission list at a specified index, defining the target, access type, and name associated with the permission.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method modifies an Access Control Entry (ACE) at a specified index within a list, updating its access type and mode. It may throw a `PermissionDeniedException` if the operation is not permitted.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method modifies an Access Control Entry (ACE) at a specified index within a permission structure. It updates the access type and mode for that ACE. The operation may fail if the caller lacks the necessary permissions.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: Removes an Access Control Entry (ACE) from a list at the specified index.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method removes all ACEs from the system, which control access permissions. It can fail if the current user lacks the necessary privileges.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method compares the current access control list (ACL) permissions against another ACL to determine if they are identical.
Return value description: Returns 'true' if the ACL permissions are exactly the same as the provided 'other' ACL, and 'false' otherwise.

Description: This method saves the current configuration if a configuration object is present. It can throw exceptions related to configuration issues or denied permissions.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: Saves the current configuration to the database if it exists.
This method converts a string representation of file permissions into an integer representation.
Return value description: An integer representing the file permissions.

Description: This method converts a numerical file mode representation into a symbolic string representation, indicating read, write, and execute permissions for owner, group, and others.
Return value description: A 9-character string representing the symbolic file mode (e.g., 'rwxr-xr--').

Description: This method converts an integer representation of file type permissions into a human-readable string.
Return value description: A string representing the file type permissions.

Description: This method calculates a file mode by combining the provided mode with execute permissions for the owner, group, and others, based on read and write permissions.
Return value description: An integer representing the modified file mode with execute permissions potentially added.

Description: This method determines if a given user has the necessary permissions to access a resource in a specific mode. It checks against the user's roles, ownership, group membership, and general access rights, returning true if the user meets any of the criteria for the requested mode.
Return value description: Returns true if the user possesses the requested access mode for the resource, and false otherwise.

Description: This method reads a long integer value from an input stream and stores it in the `vector` field.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method writes a long integer value to an output stream. It is used to serialize the internal state of an object for storage or transmission.

This method combines user ID, group ID, and resource permissions into a single 52-bit integer value. It ensures that the input IDs and permissions are within their defined bit limits before encoding them.
Return value description: A 64-bit long integer representing a bit vector that encodes user ID, group ID, and resource permissions (user, group, and other modes, along with set UID, set GID, and sticky bits).

Description: Creates a new instance of UnixStylePermission with the same security manager and permission vector as the original.
Return value description: A new UnixStylePermission object that is a copy of the original.

Description: Verifies if the current user, represented by their account, has the necessary permissions to modify a specific account. If permissions are insufficient, it throws a PermissionDeniedException.
Return value description: This method does not return any value. Its purpose is to perform an assertion and potentially throw an exception.

Description: This method validates provided credentials against stored credentials, returning true if they match and false otherwise. It leverages an external credential checking mechanism.
Return value description: A boolean value indicating whether the provided credentials are valid (true) or not (false).

Description: This method adds a new group to the system by first attempting to find an existing group with the given name within the current realm and then, if not found, searching in other connected realms. If a group is found or created, it is then added to the system.
Return value description: The method returns the Group object that was added to the system.

Description: This method adds a new group based on configuration properties. It first checks if the provided configuration object is valid and if it contains a 'name' property. If both conditions are met, it proceeds to add the group using the extracted name.
Return value description: Returns a Group object representing the newly added group, or null if the configuration is null or missing a name property.

Description: This method adds a new group to the system if the current user has the necessary permissions to modify it. It also updates an internal flag if the added group is designated as the DBA group.
Return value description: The method returns the group object that was added to the system, or null if a null group was provided.
Technique 1: Database call to retrieve the current user's account.
Technique 2: Internal data structure manipulation for adding and checking group existence.

Description: This method removes a specified group from a collection of groups associated with an account, provided the account has the necessary permissions and is not attempting to remove the last remaining group or the primary group.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Database call to retrieve account information.
Technique 2: In-memory data structure manipulation (removing from a list).

Description: Checks if a group with the specified name exists within a collection of groups.
Return value description: Returns true if a group with the given name is found, otherwise returns false.

Description: This method checks if the current user possesses the database administrator (DBA) role.
Return value description: Returns true if the user has the DBA role, and false otherwise.

Description: This method clears all stored metadata, if any exists.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method determines if a given user has the necessary permissions to modify a specific account. It enforces that either the user must have a database administrator role or be the owner of the account they are trying to modify. If the user lacks these permissions, a `PermissionDeniedException` is thrown.
This method attaches a transaction to a database broker, enabling operations within the context of that transaction. It may throw an exception if the attachment process fails.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method provides access to the application's database.
Return value description: An instance of the Database class, representing the connection to the application's database.

Description: This method registers a new user account within the system, likely by persisting the provided account details.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method registers a new group within the system.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: Verifies if an account with the given name exists.
Return value description: Returns true if an account with the specified name is found, and false otherwise.

Description: This method adds a new user account, returning the created account if successful. It may throw exceptions if the user does not have the necessary permissions or if the account already exists.
Return value description: The newly created user account.

Description: This method adds a new account to the system.
Return value description: Returns the newly added account object.

Description: This method attempts to delete a user account based on the provided name. It will throw exceptions if the current user does not have the necessary permissions or if an internal error occurs during the deletion process.
Return value description: Returns true if the account was successfully deleted, and false otherwise.

Description: This method removes a user account from the system after verifying the user has the necessary permissions. It may throw exceptions if permissions are insufficient or if an error occurs during the deletion process within the underlying system.
Return value description: Returns true if the account was successfully deleted, and false otherwise. (Note: The current implementation actually throws exceptions on failure, so a false return value is unlikely unless the method is modified.)

Description: This method updates an existing account within the system. It may throw exceptions if the user lacks the necessary permissions or if an error occurs during the update process.
Return value description: Returns true if the account was successfully updated, and false otherwise.

Description: Updates an existing group with new details.
Return value description: Returns true if the group was successfully updated, otherwise may throw an exception.

Description: This method adds a new group to the system, ensuring that the user making the request has the necessary permissions and that the group does not already exist.
Return value description: The newly created group object is returned.

Description: This method adds a new group to the system.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: Checks if a group with the given name exists.
Return value description: Returns true if the group exists, and false otherwise.

Description: This method checks if a given group exists within the system.
Return value description: Returns true if the group is found, and false otherwise.

Description: This method attempts to remove a group from the system based on its name. It may throw exceptions if the user lacks permissions or if an error occurs during the deletion process.
Return value description: Returns true if the group was successfully deleted, and false otherwise.

Description: This method determines if a given account possesses administrative privileges.
Return value description: Returns true if the account has administrative privileges, false otherwise.

Description: This method attempts to authenticate a user based on their username and provided credentials.
Return value description: It returns a Subject object representing the authenticated user if successful, or throws an AuthenticationException if authentication fails.

Description: This method registers a user's session, likely to track active users or manage their access to the system.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method checks if a group with the specified ID exists.
Return value description: Returns true if a group with the given ID is found, and false otherwise.

Description: Checks if a user with the specified ID exists in the system.
Return value description: Returns true if a user with the given ID exists, and false otherwise.

Description: Retrieves a list of usernames from the system whose personal names begin with a specified string.
Return value description: A list of strings, where each string is a username matching the provided starting characters.

Description: Retrieves a list of usernames from the system where the username begins with a specified prefix.
Return value description: A list containing strings, where each string is a username that matches the provided starting prefix.

Description: This method retrieves a list of all group names that are visible to the user who is making the request.
Return value description: A list of strings, where each string represents the name of a group visible to the invoking user.

Description: This method retrieves a list of all user names that are visible to the currently authenticated user.
Return value description: A list of strings, where each string is a user's name.

Description: This method searches for group names that begin with a specified prefix.
Return value description: A list of group names that match the provided starting string.

Description: Retrieves a list of user identifiers for all members associated with a given group name.
Return value description: A list of strings, where each string represents a unique identifier for a user who is a member of the specified group.

Description: Processes a document, potentially creating a new sub-instance, and handles configuration errors.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method prepares a document for saving by processing its parameters, potentially interacting with a database to retrieve or update information, and may throw a configuration exception if issues arise during this process.
This method retrieves a list of group names that contain a specified text fragment.
Return value description: A list of strings, where each string is a group name that includes the provided fragment.

Description: Retrieves a list of usernames from the system where the username begins with a specified string.
Return value description: A list of strings, where each string is a username that matches the specified starting pattern.

Description: This method allocates a principal based on a provided identifier.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method pre-allocates a new account identifier and provides it to a receiver. It might encounter issues if the user lacks necessary permissions or if there's an error interacting with the eXist-db.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method reserves a unique identifier for a new group. It handles potential errors related to database operations and user permissions.
This method changes the owner and group of a resource within the database, adhering to POSIX.1-2017 standards. The changes are then persisted to the database.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Database call to update resource permissions.

Description: This method changes the owner and group of a database collection according to POSIX.1-2017 standards. It updates the collection's permissions but does not persist these changes in the database.
This method changes the owner and group of a document according to POSIX.1-2017 standards. It operates on a database document, but does not save the changes.

Changes the owner and/or group of a permission based on provided owner and group strings, enforcing security restrictions based on the current subject's privileges and system configuration. This method directly modifies the permission object and may clear set-user-ID and set-group-ID bits if the current subject is not a DBA.
Technique 1: Database call to retrieve configuration properties.
Technique 2: Database call to retrieve group information.
Technique 3: Checks current subject's ownership and group membership.

Description: This method changes the mode and Access Control List (ACL) of a resource stored in the database, adhering to POSIX permissions, and persists these changes.
Technique 1: Database call to update resource permissions.

Description: This method changes the mode and access control list (ACL) of a collection in the database according to POSIX.1-2017 standards. It does not persist these changes.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method updates the permissions of a document in the database according to POSIX.1-2017 standards. It does not persist these changes. The method is designed to be used internally and does not handle persistence itself.

This method modifies the access control permissions and mode of a specified resource within the database, adhering to POSIX.1-2017 standards. It first retrieves the current permissions for the resource and then applies the requested changes based on the provided mode and Access Control Entry (ACE) list.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method modifies the access control mode and Access Control Entry (ACE) list for a database collection, enforcing POSIX.1-2017 standards.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: Updates a document's mode and access control list (ACL) in the database according to POSIX standards. This operation may fail if the calling process lacks the necessary permissions.
Technique 3: Handling optional parameters for mode and ACL

Description: This method updates the permissions and access control list (ACL) for a given permission entry in the database, adhering to POSIX.1-2017 standards.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method adjusts permission modes and Access Control Lists (ACLs) in the database according to POSIX.1-2017 standards.

This method modifies the Access Control List (ACL) of a permissioned object within the database, adhering to POSIX.1-2017 chmod rules. It applies modifications based on provided rules and throws an exception if the caller lacks the necessary permissions.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method modifies the Access Control List (ACL) permissions for a specified resource in the database, adhering to POSIX.1-2017 chmod rules. It applies a provided function to update the ACL, ensuring that only ACL-like permissions are modified. The operation is performed within a database transaction.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method modifies the Access Control List (ACL) permissions for a given resource. It ensures that only the owner of the resource or a user with database administrator privileges can perform this modification.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 2: Permission check against database administrator status

Description: Compares this group to another group based on their names. If the other object is not a GroupImpl, it throws an exception.
Return value description: Returns a negative integer, zero, or a positive integer as this group's name is lexicographically less than, equal to, or greater than the other group's name.

Description: This method checks if a given user account has the necessary permissions to modify a group. If the user is null, or does not have DBA role, or is not a manager of the group, it throws a `PermissionDeniedException`.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method adds a new manager to a list if one with the same name does not already exist. It checks for existing managers by iterating through a collection of references and compares account names.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method adds a manager to a group, provided the current user has the necessary permissions. It first retrieves the active subject from the database and then calls an internal method to perform the addition.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.
Technique 1: Database call to retrieve active subject.
Technique 2: Internal method call for adding the manager.

Description: This method adds a list of accounts as managers. It iterates through the provided list of managers and adds each one individually.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method adds a new manager to a group, ensuring the user has the necessary permissions and that the manager is not already present. If the manager already exists, the method returns without making any changes.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Database call to retrieve the active subject.
Technique 2: Permission check to ensure the current subject can modify the group.

Description: Adds a new security manager to a group at a specified index, provided the current user has permission and the manager is not already present. If the manager already exists, the operation is a no-op. This method is invoked by the Configurator component.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Database call to retrieve security context.
Technique 2: Authorization check against the current user's permissions.

Description: This method removes a specified account from the list of managers for a group, provided the current subject has the necessary permissions.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This operation clears all stored metadata.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method searches through a predefined set of schema types to find one that matches a given namespace identifier. If a match is found, it returns the corresponding schema type. If no match is found after checking all available types, it returns null.
Return value description: An EXistSchemaType object if a schema type matching the provided namespace is found, otherwise null.

Description: This method retrieves a specific schema type based on its alias.
Return value description: It returns the EXistSchemaType object that matches the provided alias, or null if no match is found.

Description: This method validates the provided credentials.
Return value description: Returns true if the credentials are valid, and false otherwise.

Description: This method retrieves a specific schema type based on a provided namespace string.
Return value description: Returns an AXSchemaType object if a match is found for the given namespace, otherwise returns null.

Description: This method finds and returns an AXSchemaType based on a provided alias string.
Return value description: An AXSchemaType object that matches the given alias, or null if no match is found.

Description: This method adds a manager to an account. It may throw an exception if the current user does not have the necessary permissions.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method adds a list of manager accounts to the system, potentially throwing an exception if the caller lacks the necessary permissions.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method removes a manager from an account if the caller has the necessary permissions.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: Validates if the given account has permission to modify a group. If not, it throws a PermissionDeniedException.
Return value description: None

Description: This method saves the current configuration, potentially throwing exceptions if the configuration is invalid or if the user lacks the necessary permissions.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method saves data using a database broker, potentially throwing exceptions related to configuration or permission issues.
This method removes all metadata associated with an object.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method generates an MD5 hash of a given message. The output can be encoded as a Base64 string or a hexadecimal string.
Return value description: A String representing the MD5 hash of the input message, either in Base64 or hexadecimal format.

Description: This method computes a cryptographic hash of a given message using a specified algorithm and returns the result as a Base64 encoded string or a hexadecimal string.
Return value description: A string representing the computed hash of the input message. The format of the hash string is either Base64 encoded or hexadecimal, depending on the `base64` parameter.

Description: This method converts a byte array into a hexadecimal string representation. It iterates through each byte of the input array and appends its hexadecimal equivalent to a string builder.
Return value description: The method returns a String representing the hexadecimal conversion of the input byte array.

Description: This method generates a hexadecimal string digest based on a username, realm ID, and a provided string, likely for security or identification purposes.
Return value description: A hexadecimal string representing the digest of the input parameters.

Description: This method takes a string, hashes it, and then encodes the resulting hash into a Base64 string.
Return value description: A Base64 encoded string representing the hash of the input string.

Description: This method generates a byte array representing the hash of an input string using a specified hashing algorithm.
Return value description: A byte array containing the computed hash of the input string, or null if the algorithm is not supported.

Description: This method computes the RIPEMD-160 hash of a given string. It utilizes cryptographic hashing algorithms to generate a fixed-size digest of the input data.
Return value description: A byte array representing the RIPEMD-160 hash of the input string.

Description: This method calculates the MD5 hash of a given string. It utilizes the Bouncy Castle cryptography library for the hashing process.
Return value description: A byte array representing the calculated MD5 hash.

Description: This method checks if the provided credentials match the expected credentials, supporting various types such as the object itself, null, Password objects, Strings, and character arrays. It aims to provide a flexible way to validate credentials against stored ones.
Return value description: Returns true if the credentials match, and false otherwise.

Description: This method initializes the system by creating administrator and guest user accounts if they do not already exist. If a 'PermissionDeniedException' occurs during this process and the system is not in 'export-only' mode, it rethrows the exception as an 'EXistException'.

This method deletes a user account. It first checks if the account exists and if the current user has the necessary permissions to delete it. If all checks pass, it marks the account as removed in the database and removes its associated XML resource.
Return value description: Returns `true` if the account was successfully processed for deletion, and `false` if the provided account was null. The method can also throw exceptions for permission denials or if the account does not exist.

Description: This method deletes a specified group from the system after performing several validation checks. It ensures the group exists, is not a system-reserved group, and is not the primary group for any active user. The method marks the group as removed and removes its associated resource from the database.
Return value description: Returns true if the group deletion process was initiated (though actual success depends on transactional commit), and false if the input group was null.

Description: This method attempts to authenticate a user based on their account name and credentials. It verifies if the account exists, is enabled, and then checks if the provided credentials match the account's stored credentials. Specific system and guest accounts are disallowed for authentication.
Return value description: Returns a Subject object representing the authenticated user if the authentication is successful.
Technique 1: Database call to retrieve account information.
Technique 2: Internal object creation for representing authenticated sessions.

Description: This method retrieves a list of usernames from a principal database that begin with a specified prefix.
Return value description: A list of usernames matching the provided prefix.

Description: This method retrieves a list of group names from a database that begin with a specified prefix.
Return value description: A list of strings, where each string is a group name that starts with the provided prefix.

Description: This method retrieves a list of group names from a database that contain a specified text fragment.
Return value description: A collection of strings, where each string is a group name that includes the provided fragment.

Description: This method retrieves a list of all group names currently stored in the system.
Return value description: A list of strings, where each string is the name of a group.

Description: This method retrieves a list of all user names from the system's principal database.
Return value description: A list of strings, where each string is a unique user name.

Description: This method retrieves a list of all user names belonging to a specified group.
Return value description: A list of strings, where each string is the name of a user in the given group.

Description: This method is intended to find usernames where the user's personal name starts with a specified string. Currently, it is a placeholder and does not return any actual usernames, as user personal name details are not stored in the system at this time. Its primary use is within the LDAP realm.
Return value description: An empty list of strings, representing usernames that match the given starting string. In its current state, this list will always be empty.

Description: This method is intended to retrieve a list of usernames where the username begins with a specified string. However, it is currently a placeholder that always returns an empty list, as user name details are not yet implemented and this functionality is associated with an LDAP realm.
Return value description: An empty list of strings, representing usernames.

Description: This method is intended to authenticate a user based on provided credentials. Currently, it is implemented to always return false, indicating that authentication will always fail.
Return value description: Returns false, signifying that authentication is unsuccessful.

Description: This method handles authentication events based on the provided subject. If authentication has not been previously established, it runs a script to perform authentication. Otherwise, it delegates the event handling to an existing authentication mechanism.
Return value description: The method returns void.

Description: This method executes a specified XQuery script with given arguments, retrieving data from a database and handling potential errors during execution. It sets up the execution context, compiles the query, and then invokes a user-defined function within that query.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Database access to retrieve query sources and manage broker connections.
Technique 2: XQuery execution, including compilation and invocation of user-defined functions.
Technique 3: Resource management for database brokers and query contexts.

Description: This method is triggered when an event occurs related to a subject. It executes a predefined script associated with that subject.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method initializes the login module by storing the provided subject, callback handler, and configuration options. It also sets a debug flag based on the configuration.
Technique 2: Setting internal state based on input parameters

Description: This method authenticates a user by prompting for their username and password, then verifying these credentials against the system's security manager. If authentication is successful, it returns true; otherwise, it throws an exception.
Return value description: Returns true if the user is successfully authenticated.
Technique 1: Interacting with the user to get credentials.
Technique 2: Calling the security manager to authenticate the user.
Technique 3: Handling potential IO and callback exceptions.

Description: This method is invoked after an overall authentication attempt succeeds. It associates an authenticated identity with the user's subject if the module's own login was successful, or cleans up any saved state if the login failed.
Return value description: Returns true if this module's login and commit operations were successful, and false otherwise.

Description: This method handles the cleanup of authentication state when the overall authentication process fails, potentially rolling back specific login module actions if its own authentication was successful.
Return value description: Returns `false` if the module's login or commit attempts failed, and `true` otherwise, indicating the state of the abort operation.

Description: This method logs out a user by removing their principal information from the subject and clearing the user principal reference. It is designed to always succeed and not be ignored.
Return value description: The method always returns true, indicating that the logout operation was attempted and should not be ignored.

Description: This method verifies user credentials against an account. It sets an internal flag indicating whether the authentication was successful and returns this status.
Return value description: Returns a boolean indicating whether the authentication was successful.

Description: This method initializes the security context by creating a default realm, a system subject, and a guest subject. It also adds the default realm to a collection of realms.
Return value description: None.
Technique 2: Lazy initialization of subjects using AtomicLazyVal.

Description: This method initiates the system by attaching the provided database broker and transaction. It handles potential exceptions during the attachment process by re-throwing them as a BrokerPoolServiceException.
This method initiates a recurring background task that periodically checks for and handles expired user sessions.
Technique 2: Using a database broker for system operations

Description: This method initializes the security manager by ensuring that the '/db/system' and '/db/system/security' collections exist within the database. If these collections do not exist, they are created with default permissions and configurations. It then loads and applies security configurations, and starts all defined security realms.
Technique 1: Database call to get and create collections.

Description: This method updates an existing account. It first checks if the account and its realm ID are valid. If they are, it acquires a write lock for the account before proceeding with the update operation via the associated realm. If the account is null, the method returns false. If the realm ID is missing, it throws a configuration exception.
Return value description: Returns true if the account was successfully updated, and false if the provided account was null.
Technique 1: Database call: The method interacts with a database to find a realm based on its ID and then updates the account within that realm.
Technique 2: Locking: A write lock is acquired to ensure exclusive access to the account during the update process, preventing concurrent modifications.

Description: This method updates an existing group within a specific realm. It ensures the group has a realm identifier before proceeding with the update. If the group is null, no update is performed.
Return value description: Returns true if the group was successfully updated, and false if the group object was null and therefore no update was attempted.
Technique 1: Managed locking for write operations to ensure data consistency.
Technique 2: Database call to find the realm associated with the group.
Technique 3: Database call to update the group's information.

Description: This method deletes a specified group from the system after ensuring it exists and has an associated realm ID. It utilizes a write lock to safely perform the deletion operation.
Return value description: Returns true if the group was successfully deleted, and false if the group was not found.

Initializes the servlet by retrieving configuration parameters for an XQuery, default user credentials, and a collection Uniform Resource Identifier (URI). It validates the provided URI and sets default values if parameters are missing or invalid, preparing the servlet for operation.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method processes an incoming HTTP request by executing an XQuery. The result of the XQuery determines the next action, which could be a redirect to a new URL, a dispatch to another servlet, or an error response if the query result is invalid.
Return value description: This method does not return a value, but it modifies the HTTP response by either sending an error, a redirect, or forwarding the request to another resource.

Description: This method adds a parameter with a given name and value to a collection of parameters.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method regenerates the session identifier for the current user's request.
Return value description: The newly generated session identifier string.

Description: This method handles the authentication of a request, delegating the actual authentication process to an underlying request object and returning a boolean indicating success or failure.
Return value description: Returns true if the authentication was successful, and false otherwise.

Description: Authenticates a user with the provided username and password.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method invalidates the current user's session, effectively logging them out of the system.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method handles the upgrade of an HTTP request to a different protocol, such as WebSockets, by delegating to the underlying request object.
Return value description: It returns an instance of the specified `HttpUpgradeHandler` class, which represents the upgraded connection.

Description: This method removes an attribute from the current HTTP request.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method initiates asynchronous request processing. It delegates the actual start of asynchronous operation to the underlying HttpServletRequest.
Return value description: An AsyncContext object is returned, which can be used to manage the asynchronous operation.

Description: This method initiates asynchronous processing for an incoming web request and its corresponding response.
Return value description: An AsyncContext object is returned, which can be used to manage the asynchronous operations.

Description: This method closes an input stream and its associated cache, releasing associated resources. This is typically done when the stream is no longer needed to prevent resource leaks.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: Reads a single byte of data from the input stream.
Return value description: The byte of data read from the input stream, or -1 if the end of the stream has been reached.

Description: Reads data from an input stream into a byte array.
Return value description: Returns the number of bytes read, or -1 if the end of the stream has been reached.

Description: This method reads a specified number of bytes from an input stream into a byte array, starting at a given offset. It acts as a pass-through for the underlying input stream's read functionality.
Return value description: The number of bytes actually read into the buffer, or -1 if the end of the stream has been reached.

Description: This method reports the number of bytes that can be read from the input stream without blocking.
Return value description: An integer representing the number of bytes available to be read.

Description: This method initializes the REST server, configuring its behavior based on servlet parameters related to dynamic content types and feature enablement for XQuery and XUpdate submissions. It also performs checks on the XML library.

This method handles HTTP PUT requests to update or create resources. It first adjusts and potentially maps the request path, then authenticates the user. Finally, it attempts to process the request by interacting with a database collection, committing or aborting a transaction, and sending an appropriate HTTP response or error.
Return value description: This method does not return a value; it modifies the HttpServletResponse.

Description: This method handles HTTP PATCH requests. It authenticates the user, processes the request against a database path, and commits or aborts the transaction based on the outcome. It returns appropriate HTTP error codes for various exceptional conditions.
Return value description: This method does not return a value, but it sends an HTTP response to the client indicating success or failure.

Description: This method handles incoming GET requests by adjusting the path, optionally logging and mapping it based on a descriptor, authenticating the user, and then processing the request using a database broker and transaction. It returns appropriate HTTP error responses for various exceptions like bad requests, permission denials, or resource not found.
Return value description: The method does not explicitly return a value, but it modifies the HttpServletResponse by sending data or error codes.
Technique 1: Database call is made using DBBroker.
Technique 2: HTTP call is made to send error responses or authentication challenges.

Description: This method handles HEAD requests by adjusting the path, optionally logging and mapping it based on a descriptor, authenticating the user, and then processing the request using a database broker and transaction. It manages various exceptions during processing, including bad requests, permission denials, not found errors, and internal server errors.
Return value description: This method does not return any value, but it modifies the HttpServletResponse by sending appropriate error codes or committing the response.

Description: This method handles the deletion of a resource by first adjusting the path, then mapping it if a descriptor is present, authenticating the user, and finally processing the delete request using a database broker and transaction. It also handles various exceptions related to permissions, resource not found, and internal server errors.
Return value description: This method does not return a value, but it modifies the HttpServletResponse by sending back status codes and error messages.

Description: This method handles POST requests by processing the request path, logging it if configured, mapping the path, authenticating the user, and then executing the core POST logic using a database transaction. It also manages various exceptions that may occur during request processing, returning appropriate HTTP error responses.
Return value description: This method does not return a value; it modifies the HttpServletResponse object directly or throws exceptions.

Description: This method handles incoming HTTP requests. It specifically intercepts PATCH requests to delegate them to a dedicated handler, otherwise, it passes the request to the default service implementation.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method attempts to authenticate a user based on provided credentials in the request's Authorization header. It verifies the username and password against the security manager. If authentication fails or is incomplete, it may send a challenge back to the client.
Return value description: Returns a Subject object representing the authenticated user, or null if authentication fails or credentials are not provided.
Technique 2: Writes to the HTTP response (sending challenge).
Technique 3: Database call to retrieve user account information.

Description: This method sends an HTTP unauthorized response to the client, initiating a digest authentication challenge. It sets the 'WWW-Authenticate' header with details required for the client to generate a response, including a realm, a nonce, a domain, and an opaque value.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method verifies user credentials against a provided response, commonly used for authentication challenges.
Return value description: Returns true if the credentials are valid for the given challenge, and false otherwise. It also returns true if no credentials are set, indicating an unauthenticated state.
Technique 1: Cryptographic hashing (MD5) is used to process credentials.
Technique 2: String manipulation and byte array conversions are performed.

Description: This method handles user authentication by first checking for existing session credentials. If no valid session exists or if the username doesn't match, it attempts to authenticate the user using Basic Authentication credentials from the request header. If authentication fails or credentials are not provided, it may prompt the user for credentials.
Return value description: Returns a Subject object representing the authenticated user, or null if authentication is not successful or if a challenge needs to be sent to the client.

Description: This method sends an HTTP unauthorized response to a client, including a 'WWW-Authenticate' header to prompt for basic authentication credentials. This is typically done when a client attempts to access a protected resource without providing valid authentication information.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method is invoked when a user's session is created. It logs the session ID and then executes an XQuery script located at a path specified by a system property.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method is triggered when an HTTP session is destroyed. It logs information about the destroyed session and then executes an XQuery script.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method writes an HTTP response to an output stream. It constructs the response headers including the status code, status description, content type, and content length, followed by the response body if present. Finally, it flushes and closes the output stream.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method retrieves the stored string value.
Return value description: The current string value that was previously set.

Description: This method returns an enumeration value based on a provided string. If the string does not match any enumeration values, it throws an exception.
Return value description: An enumeration value of type YesNo.

Description: This method generates and returns a new instance of a Query object.
Return value description: A new, empty Query object.

Description: This method is responsible for creating and returning a new instance of a Result object.
Return value description: An instance of the Result class.

Description: This method creates and returns a new Sequence object.
Return value description: A newly instantiated Sequence object.

Description: This method creates and returns a new instance of Query.Properties.
Return value description: A new Query.Properties object.

Description: This method creates and returns a new instance of Query Variables.
Return value description: A new Query.Variables object is returned.

Description: This method constructs and returns a new variable object intended for use within a query structure.
Return value description: A new instance of `Query.Variables.Variable`.

Description: This method is responsible for generating a new, empty instance of a Collection object.
Return value description: A new instance of the Collection class.

Description: This method is responsible for creating and returning a new instance of a Result Value object.
Return value description: A newly created instance of Result.Value.

Description: This method generates and returns a new instance of Sequence.Value, which is used to represent a value within a sequence.
Return value description: A newly created Sequence.Value object.

Description: This method constructs and returns a new `Property` object, which is a component used to define properties within a query structure.
Return value description: A new `Query.Properties.Property` object, ready to be configured with specific query property details.

Description: This method creates and returns a new instance of a Qname object, which is a type of variable used in queries.
Return value description: An instance of the Query.Variables.Variable.Qname class, representing a qualified name for a query variable.

Description: This method stores a query and its associated sequence in a cache, returning a unique session identifier for the stored data.
Return value description: The integer returned is a unique session identifier that can be used to retrieve the previously stored query and sequence.

Description: This method releases a session by invalidating its entry in the cache, but only if the session ID is within a valid range.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method deactivates the filter, making it unavailable for processing requests. It performs internal state cleanup by removing its configuration.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method logs detailed information about an incoming HTTP request and its associated components, including parameters, headers, cookies, and various request properties, before passing the request along to the next filter in the chain. If logging is disabled, it bypasses all logging and directly proceeds to the next filter.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method initializes a filter by storing its configuration for later use.
Return value description: None

Description: Initializes the filter with the provided configuration.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method inspects incoming HTTP requests and, based on certain conditions related to the request's query parameters, URI, or HTTP method, it either allows the request to proceed through the filter chain or denies it by sending an error response.
Return value description: The method does not return a value; it modifies the response or passes the request along the filter chain.

Description: This method deallocates resources by setting internal fields to null, effectively clearing the state of the object.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method initializes the filter, logging a starting message and storing the filter configuration for later use.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method acts as a security filter, intercepting incoming HTTP requests to enforce access controls and redirect to secure connections. It checks if the request is for a WebDAV resource and if the user is authenticated, preventing guest access to these resources. It also ensures that requests are made over HTTPS, redirecting to a secure URL if not.
Return value description: This method does not return any value directly, but it may forward the request to the next filter in the chain, send an error response, or redirect the client to a different URL.

Description: This method logs a message indicating the end of the GuestFilter.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method generates a URL query string parameter key by prepending an underscore to an XML key.
Return value description: Returns a string representing a parameter key suitable for use in a URL query string.

Description: This method generates an XML-safe key from a given name by converting it to lowercase and replacing underscores with hyphens.
Return value description: A string representing the parameter key, formatted for use as an element or attribute name in an XML document.

Description: This method handles GET requests by serving documents or binary resources, listing collection contents, or executing XQuery/XProc scripts based on the provided path. It also supports various parameters for querying, controlling output formatting, and specifying XSL stylesheets.
Return value description: This method returns resources, collection listings, or the results of XQuery/XProc executions to the client via an HttpServletResponse.
Technique 1: Database calls to retrieve and lock resources, open collections, and execute queries.
Technique 2: HTTP calls are implicitly made to handle the incoming GET request and send back the response.
Technique 3: XML parsing and serialization for handling XQuery scripts, variables, and output formatting.

Description: This method retrieves information about a resource or collection located at a given path and sets appropriate HTTP headers in the response. It checks for read permissions and determines the content type and modification dates to include in the response headers.
Return value description: This method does not return any value, but it modifies the HttpServletResponse by setting headers and potentially sending an error.

Description: This method handles POST requests by executing XQuery or XProc scripts if the requested resource is of the correct MIME type. Otherwise, it processes the request content as either an XML document containing an XQuery or an XUpdate statement, or delegates to a GET request if the content type is URL-encoded.
Return value description: This method does not return a value directly. It writes the result of the operation to the provided HttpServletResponse object.
Technique 2: Parsing XML content from the request.

Description: This method records a namespace declaration encountered during XML parsing, but only if it's not the 'exist' namespace. It adds the namespace to a collection for later use. It also ensures the standard SAX event processing continues.

This method handles PUT requests to store a new resource at a specified location. If the resource already exists, it is overwritten if the user has the necessary write permissions. The type of resource stored is determined by the `Content-Type` header, defaulting to binary if the MIME type is not recognized as XML.
This method handles PATCH requests, specifically for XQuery modules. If the target resource is not an XQuery module, it prevents the request from proceeding.

This method deletes a collection or a document from the database based on the provided path. It checks for necessary permissions and handles exceptions for not found resources, permission denials, or bad requests.

This method executes an XQuery against a database, optionally retrieving cached results, handling security checks, and returning the query output. It supports caching of query results and manages XQuery compilation and execution.
Return value description: This method does not return a value directly; instead, it writes the query results to the HttpServletResponse.

Description: This method serializes the contents of a collection, including sub-collections and documents, into an XML format and writes it to an HTTP response. It includes metadata such as creation dates, last modified dates, and permissions for each item.
Return value description: This method does not return a value. It directly writes to the provided HttpServletResponse.
Technique 1: Database call: retrieves collection and document metadata from the database.
Technique 2: HTTP call: writes serialized XML data to the HTTP response.
Technique 3: XML Serialization: uses a SAXSerializer to construct the XML output.

Description: This method adds owner, group, and permission details as attributes to an XML attributes object based on a provided permission object.
Return value description: This method does not return a value directly. It modifies the passed-in AttributesImpl object by adding attributes.

Description: This method writes query results to an HTTP response. It first checks if the response has already been committed, and if not, it calculates the number of results to return based on the 'start' and 'howmany' parameters. Finally, it delegates the actual writing of the results to either a JSON or XML serialization method based on the 'serialization-method' property.
Return value description: This method does not return a value; it writes directly to the HTTP response stream.

Description: This method removes a specified path prefix from an incoming request if a prefix has been configured.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method is intended to be overridden by subclasses to provide custom logic for rewriting incoming HTTP requests. By default, it performs no action.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method determines if a path is relative. It returns true if the path is not absolute, and false otherwise.
Return value description: A boolean value indicating whether the path is relative (true) or absolute (false).

Description: This method determines the final destination path for a request based on a rewrite rule and the current request's context. It handles cases where no rewrite rule is defined, or when the rule needs to be combined with the request's base path to form a complete target. The process involves resolving the target against the request's URI, potentially correcting for relative paths.
Return value description: The method returns the computed target path, which represents the resolved destination for the request, excluding any context path.
Technique 3: Exception handling for invalid URI syntax.

Description: This method copies headers, attributes, and parameters from another URLRewrite object into the current one, creating new mutable collections for each to ensure independent modification.
Return value description: void, this method does not return a value.

Description: This method creates and returns a copy of the current URL rewrite configuration.
Return value description: A new instance of URLRewrite that is a duplicate of the current object.

Description: This method processes an incoming HTTP request and generates an HTTP response, potentially involving modifications or a complete rewrite of the request or response lifecycle. It is designed to be implemented by subclasses to define specific rewriting logic.
Return value description: This method does not return a value directly. Its effects are realized through the modification of the HttpServletResponse object.

Description: This method prepares a request by adding parameters and attributes to it. It iterates through a collection of parameters and adds each one as a key-value pair to the request. It also iterates through a collection of attributes, setting or removing them from the request based on their value.
Technique 1: Iterates through a map of parameters.
Technique 2: Iterates through a map of attributes.

Description: This method cleans up a given string representing a path by removing redundant forward slashes. It ensures that there is only a single forward slash between path segments and at the beginning if the path starts with a slash.
Return value description: A normalized string representing the cleaned-up path.

Description: This method handles the rewriting of HTTP requests and responses.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method updates the request's context path by prepending a target path, unless the target path is empty, is a root path, or represents an XML DB URI.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.
Technique 3: Conditional logic based on path characteristics.

Description: This method rewrites an incoming request based on a target URI, potentially to map external URIs to internal RESTful endpoints. It modifies the request's path and base path to conform to a '/rest' structure, adjusting for collection paths and context paths. An attribute is also set on the request to indicate that a rewrite has occurred.
This method creates a new instance of `ControllerForward`, effectively duplicating the current `URLRewrite` object.
Return value description: A new `ControllerForward` object that is a copy of the original `URLRewrite` object.

Description: This method creates and returns a new URL rewrite configuration that passes through the original URL without modification.
Return value description: A new URL rewrite configuration object that mirrors the current one but operates in a pass-through mode.

Description: This method handles incoming HTTP requests, configures response headers, and forwards the request to a designated resource.
This method finds a URL rewrite rule based on the request's path and server name.
Return value description: It returns a URLRewrite object representing the matching rule, or null if no rule is found.

Description: This method looks up a given path within a collection of defined mappings. It searches for a matching mapping based on the provided path and server name, and returns the associated action if found. The method also handles optional copying of configuration from an existing action and filters results based on whether only static mappings are requested.
Return value description: Returns a URLRewrite instance representing the found mapping, or null if no matching mapping is discovered.

Description: This method attempts to match a given path against a predefined pattern and returns the matched portion of the path if successful. Otherwise, it returns null.
Return value description: Returns the substring of the input path that matches the pattern, or null if no match is found.

Description: This method initializes configuration parameters for the filter, including an XQuery string, a flag for compiled cache, and a flag for sending challenges. It retrieves these parameters from the provided ServletConfig.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method processes incoming HTTP requests by applying URL rewriting rules, authenticating users, executing XQuery, and managing caching. It then dispatches the request to the appropriate handler or generates an HTTP response based on the XQuery results.
Return value description: The method does not return a value directly, but it writes to the HttpServletResponse and potentially modifies the HttpServletRequest.

Description: This method clears the URL cache.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method releases the ServletConfig object held by the class, effectively cleaning up resources.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method adjusts a given path based on a base path, primarily to remove prefixes that are specific to embedded server URIs or a common database prefix.
Return value description: The method returns the adjusted path string.

Description: This method adds a URL rewrite handler to a list of handlers. If no list of handlers exists, it first initializes an empty list.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method adds a URL rewrite rule to a collection of rules.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method checks if there are any views associated with the current object.
Return value description: Returns true if there are views, false otherwise.

Description: This method checks if there are any error handlers configured and available. It returns true if at least one error handler exists, and false otherwise.
Return value description: A boolean value indicating whether error handlers are present.

Description: This method checks if caching is enabled for the current operation.
Return value description: A boolean value indicating whether the cache is currently in use (true) or not (false).

Description: This method controls whether subsequent requests can be cached. It accepts a boolean value to enable or disable caching.
This method modifies the request's path by removing a specified prefix from it. It updates both the context path and the servlet path accordingly.
This method adds a parameter to a collection of parameters, associating a given name with a given value.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method sends an HTTP error response with a specified status code and message. It updates the internal status and then delegates the actual sending of the error to a parent class.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method sends an error status to the client and records the error code.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method flushes the buffered output to the client if caching is enabled. Otherwise, it delegates to the parent class's buffer flushing mechanism.
Return value description: None.
Technique 1: Checks a boolean flag to determine execution path.
Technique 2: Delegates to a parent class method.

Description: This method writes buffered data to the client's output stream and flushes the stream. If caching is enabled and a content type is set, it also sets the response's content type.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method writes a single byte to an output stream. It is part of a stream that buffers data in memory. This operation could potentially be a part of writing data to a file, sending data over a network, or preparing data for further processing.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: Writes a byte array to an output stream.
This method writes a specified portion of a byte array to an output stream.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Writes data to an output stream.
Technique 2: Uses an in-memory byte array buffer.

Description: This method reads a single byte from an input stream.
Return value description: Returns the next byte of data from the input stream, or -1 if the end of the stream has been reached.

Description: This method reads a sequence of bytes from an input stream into a byte array.
Return value description: Returns the total number of bytes read, or -1 if the end of the stream has been reached.

Description: This method reads a sequence of bytes from an input stream into a byte array.
Return value description: The total number of bytes read, or -1 if the end of the stream has been reached.

Description: This method returns the number of bytes that can be read from the input stream without blocking.
Return value description: An integer representing the number of bytes available for reading.

Description: Creates a copy of the current URL rewrite configuration.
Return value description: A new URL rewrite configuration object.

Description: This method evaluates an XQuery expression using context information from the incoming request. It then stores the result of the evaluation in the request attributes.
Return value description: The method does not return a value directly; instead, it modifies the HttpServletRequest by setting an attribute named 'XQueryURLRewrite.RQ_ATTR_RESULT' with the evaluated XQuery result.
Technique 1: Database call: An XQuery expression is evaluated, which implies interaction with a database or data source where the XQuery is executed.
Technique 2: HTTP Request Manipulation: The method accesses and modifies attributes of the incoming HttpServletRequest.

Description: This method creates a copy of the current URL rewrite configuration, specifically for module calls.
Return value description: A new ModuleCall object representing a copy of the current URL rewrite configuration.

Description: This method issues an HTTP redirect to a specified target URL, after setting custom response headers.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method creates and returns a new instance of a Redirect object, initialized with the state of the current URLRewrite object.
Return value description: A new Redirect object that is a copy of the current URLRewrite object.

Description: This method initializes a database instance. It does not perform any actions.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method handles the closing of a database instance. It's designed to gracefully shut down and release resources associated with a broker pool.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method registers a management bean for a specific instance. It is designed to be a no-operation method, meaning it does not perform any action when called.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method is intended to change the status of a task within a broker pool, but currently has no implementation.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method is intended to update the status of a broker pool, potentially indicating progress or completion, but currently has no implementation.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method establishes a connection to the local Java Management Extensions (JMX) instance. It attempts to locate an MBeanServer and, if found, sets it as the active connection.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: Establishes a connection to a remote JMX instance using the provided address and port, and retrieves a connection to the MBean server.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.
Technique 2: Establishes a connection to a remote JMX server.

Description: This method generates an XML report containing Java Management Extensions (JMX) data for specified categories. It compiles the requested JMX information into an XML document, which is then serialized into a string format. The available categories for the report include memory, instances, disk, system, caches, locking, processes, sanity, or all categories.
Return value description: A string containing the generated XML report.

Description: This method checks the responsiveness of a database by attempting to establish a connection and execute a simple query within a specified timeout period. It returns the response time if successful, a timeout error code if the database does not respond within the given time, or a different error code if there's an issue with the database server.
Return value description: The method returns the response time in milliseconds if the database is responsive. If the database does not respond within the specified timeout, it returns -99. If there's any other server-side error, it returns a value less than 0.

Description: This method attempts to ping an MBean using its ObjectName and returns the result. If an error occurs during the ping operation, it logs the error and returns a predefined error code.
Return value description: Returns a Long representing the result of the ping operation or an error code if the operation fails.

Description: This method retrieves Java Management Extensions (JMX) output for specified categories and formats it as an XML document. It can report on memory, instances, disk, system, caches, locking, processes, sanity, or all available categories. An optional error code can also be included in the report.
Return value description: Returns an XML Element representing the generated JMX report.
Technique 1: Internal XML document construction using MemTreeBuilder.

Description: This method invokes a specified operation on a Java Management Extensions (JMX) MBean and then serializes the result into an XML document.
Return value description: An XML Element representing the result of the JMX operation.
Technique 1: Database Call: A JMX Server connection is established to retrieve information about MBeans and their operations. This involves communication with a remote or local JMX agent.
Technique 2: HTTP Call: While not directly making an HTTP call, the serialization of the result into an XML Element implies that this XML could be transmitted over HTTP or used in a web context.
Technique 3: Reflection: The method uses reflection to dynamically invoke MBean operations based on provided names and arguments, and to introspect MBean metadata.

Description: This is the main entry point of the application. It first checks if the Java version is compatible, and if not, it exits with an error code. It then establishes a connection to a JMX service on localhost and generates a report based on the provided arguments, printing the report to the console.
Return value description: The method does not return any value as it is a void method.

Description: Establishes a connection to a remote Java Management Extensions (JMX) MBean server using the provided address and port, with default guest credentials. This allows for remote management and monitoring of the application.
Return value description: This method does not return a value. It modifies the state of the object by setting the `connection` field.

Description: This method retrieves and displays information about the Java Virtual Machine's heap memory usage, including current usage, committed memory, and maximum memory. It logs any exceptions encountered during this process.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Accessing JVM runtime information via JMX

Description: This method retrieves and displays statistics about the current instance's memory usage, broker activity, and active threads by querying the Java Management Extensions (JMX) MBean server.
Return value description: This method does not return a value; it directly prints statistics to the console.

Description: This method retrieves and displays statistics about the system's caches, including overall cache usage and details for individual caches like collection caches.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Retrieves information from a management interface (e.g., JMX).
Technique 2: Formats and prints output to the console.

Description: This method retrieves and displays information about threads currently waiting for a lock within the system. It details the lock type, mode, ID, owner, and any read or write locks being waited upon by each thread.
Return value description: This method does not return any value directly; it prints information to the console.
Technique 1: JMX (Java Management Extensions) calls to retrieve lock manager information.
Technique 2: Data retrieval from JMX attributes which are structured as TabularData and CompositeData.
Technique 3: Error handling for JMX and I/O operations.

Description: This method generates a report on the status and errors of a sanity check. It retrieves information about the sanity check's status, start and end times, and any reported errors. The report is then printed to the console.
Return value description: None, this method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Accessing Java Management Extensions (JMX) MBeans to retrieve operational data from the application.

Description: This method generates and prints a report of running jobs and queries, including their IDs, actions, and associated information. It retrieves this data by making calls to a management interface.
Return value description: This method does not return any value; it prints the report to the console.

Description: This method serves as the entry point for the JMX client application. It validates the Java version, parses command-line arguments, and then processes these arguments to perform the requested operations.
