It ensures the input string has a valid numeric value optionally followed by a memory unit (e.g., 'g', 'm', 'k'). If no unit is provided, it defaults to megabytes.
This method converts a Java command-line memory string (like '1024m' or '2g') into a format expected by prunsrv.exe, which requires memory values in megabytes.
Return value description: A string representing the memory value in megabytes, or an empty optional if the input string is invalid.

Description: This method makes messages visible and then resizes the containing panel to fit its contents.

This method updates the state of specific buttons based on notifications received from an observable source. It enables or disables the dashboard and eXide buttons depending on whether the corresponding application is being installed. If the notification is not related to these specific applications, its string representation is appended to a message display.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 2: UI updates on the Swing Event Dispatch Thread

Description: This method initializes the application by checking for a compatible Java version and then setting the native look and feel for the user interface, excluding Linux. It then launches the main application window on the event dispatch thread.

This method stops a running service. If requested, it will attempt to restart the service after stopping it. If the service is not running, it will shut down the application, optionally restarting it by launching a new process.

This method opens the application's dashboard in a web browser. It first updates a status message, then safely accesses a service to construct the dashboard's URI, and finally launches the browser with that URI.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 2: Opening a URI in the default web browser
Technique 3: Safely accessing a shared service using a lock

Description: This method opens the eXide application in a web browser after updating the status panel. It ensures that only one service operation runs at a time to prevent conflicts.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 2: Acquires a service lock to ensure exclusive access.
Technique 3: Opens a URI in the default web browser.

Description: This method initiates a client process using a LauncherWrapper.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method starts the application, enabling the stop button and disabling the start button. It then checks if the application should be installed as a Windows service and prompts the user for installation if necessary.
Technique 3: Background thread execution for UI updates

Description: This method signals that the server has stopped. It updates the system tray icon's tooltip and enables/disables menu items for starting and stopping the service, provided the server is not currently being installed as a service.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method updates the enabled state of specific menu items based on notifications received from the Exist repository. It checks the package URI of the notification and, if it matches a known package, enables or disables the corresponding menu item based on the action (e.g., INSTALL).
This method displays a message to the user in a dialog box. If a log viewing option is enabled, it will be included in the dialog.
Return value description: void, this method does not return a value.
Technique 1: Creates a graphical user interface (GUI) element.
Technique 2: Displays a modal dialog box to the user.

Description: This method attempts to open the application's log file in the default system application for text files. It first checks if the desktop environment is supported and then verifies if the log file is readable. If the file is not found or cannot be opened, an error message is displayed to the user.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.
Technique 1: File system access (reading log file existence and path)

Description: This method installs a service. If the service is already installed, an exception is thrown.
Return value description: None

Description: This method uninstalls a service, raising an exception if the service has already been uninstalled or if any other error occurs during the uninstallation process.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: Initiates the service if it is not already running. If the service is already active, this operation has no effect.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method halts the operation of a service. If the service is already in a stopped state, no action is taken. The process may result in a ServiceManagerException if any issues arise during the stopping procedure.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method displays the operating system's native service management console to the user. It may throw exceptions if the system doesn't support this functionality or if an error occurs while attempting to open the console.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method handles the initial setup and display of a dialog, either for the very first launch of the application or for subsequent launches. On the first start, it configures specific UI elements, sets a default data directory based on the operating system, and ensures relevant messages are visible. For subsequent launches, it hides certain startup messages. In both cases, it makes the dialog visible and brings it to the foreground.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Accessing system properties to determine OS and user home directory.
Technique 2: Manipulating UI element visibility and state.
Technique 3: Setting text content for UI input fields.

Description: This is the entry point for the application. It performs an initial compatibility check, parses command-line arguments, and then either launches the main application logic or presents a configuration dialog if it's the first time the application is being run. Errors encountered during startup or argument parsing are handled by printing messages to the console and exiting with an appropriate error code.
Return value description: This method does not return any value as it is the main entry point of the application and controls its lifecycle through system exit calls.

Description: This method initiates a new Java process to run the main class of the eXist application. It configures the new process with specific Java options, a classpath, and the command to be executed. If debugging is enabled, it also sets up Java Debug Wire Protocol (JDWP) for remote debugging. If an error occurs during process execution, it displays an error message to the user.
Return value description: This method returns void, indicating it does not produce a return value but rather performs an action.

Description: This method clears the cached properties, making them unavailable for subsequent use until they are reloaded.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method checks if a specific property exists within the system's configuration.
Return value description: Returns true if the property is found, and false otherwise.

Description: This method checks if a runtime property with the given name exists.
Return value description: Returns true if the property exists, false otherwise.

Description: This method stores an object in a map, associating it with a given name. If the internal map has not been initialized, it is created before storing the object.
Return value description: The previously stored object associated with the given name, or null if there was no mapping for the name.

Description: This method checks for configuration updates and applies them if the system is not in a saving state and a valid configured object is available. It clears any existing cache, updates the internal element, and then reconfigures the object.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method saves the current element if it is not an in-memory element. It synchronizes access to ensure that only one thread can save at a time and handles potential configuration errors during the save process.

This method saves a document to the database, but only if it's not an in-memory element. It also handles configuration saving if a configured object reference is present, ensuring that the saving process is synchronized and exceptions are properly handled.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method handles different events related to document management, specifically removing a document or checking for configuration updates. When a document is removed, it unregisters its associated configuration. For other events, it retrieves the configuration and checks for updates using the document's root element.
Return value description: The method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Database calls are made through DBBroker to access configuration.
Technique 2: Configuration is retrieved and updated using the Configurator class.

Description: This method initializes the trigger by setting a flag to indicate that a document is being created or updated, and it stores a reference to the database broker.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Database access is initiated via a DBBroker.

Description: This method is executed after a document is created. It checks if the document is part of a saving list and returns early if it is. Otherwise, it checks for updates to the document and, if the document is in the security collection, processes its parameters through the security manager. Finally, it resets internal state related to the broker and document creation/update status.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method is executed before a document is updated. It checks if the document is part of a saving list and, if the document resides within the security collection, it processes security-related parameters. If a configuration exception occurs during security processing, it's logged.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.
Technique 1: Checks a configuration setting to determine if a document should be processed.
Technique 2: Accesses security management to process parameters before saving a document.
Technique 3: Logs errors encountered during configuration processing.

Description: This method is executed after a document is updated. It first checks if the document is part of a saving list and returns if it is. Then, it performs an update check for the document. If the document belongs to the security collection, it processes security parameters. Finally, it clears internal state related to the broker and update status.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method is designed to be called before a document is copied. It receives database transaction and document information but currently performs no actions.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method is triggered after a document is copied and checks for any necessary updates to the document.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method is intended to be called before a document is moved within the database. It receives information about the database transaction, the document being moved, and its new location.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method is invoked after a document has been moved within the database. It checks for any necessary updates related to the moved document.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method unregisters a configuration associated with a document if a configuration exists. It's triggered before a document is deleted.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method is a callback that is invoked after a document is deleted. It does not perform any actions.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method is designed to execute logic before a document's metadata is updated within a transaction. It receives the database broker, the transaction object, and the document whose metadata is about to be modified.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method is called after a document's metadata has been updated. It receives the database broker, transaction, and the document that was updated.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method is designed to be called as part of a trigger mechanism, allowing custom logic to be executed within a database transaction. It receives transaction, database, and collection context, along with parameters for customization.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method processes the start of an XML element during parsing. It conditionally manages internal state based on the element's namespace and name, specifically looking for 'account' or 'group' elements within a 'Configuration.NS' namespace. It also tracks if an 'account' element contains a 'group' element.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method processes the end of an XML element, specifically handling the completion of an account or group definition within a configuration namespace. It triggers the processing of the completed principal, ensures accounts have a primary group, and stops deferring further XML events.
Return value description: This method has a void return type and does not return any value.

Description: This method retrieves a new ID by looking up a provided old ID in a mapping. It is designed to translate IDs from a legacy system to a new system that incorporates ACL Permissions. If an old ID is not found in the mapping, it indicates that the ID does not need migration and will not be found.
Return value description: The method returns the corresponding new ID if a mapping exists for the provided old ID. If the old ID is not found in the mapping (meaning it's not a legacy ID or doesn't require migration), it returns null.

Description: Checks if a user or group with the given name exists within the security manager based on the principal type.
Return value description: Returns true if a principal of the specified type with the given name exists, and false otherwise.

Description: This method checks if a principal (user or group) with a given ID exists within the security manager. It determines whether to check for a user or a group based on the current type.
Return value description: Returns true if the principal exists, and false otherwise.
Technique 1: Makes a call to the SecurityManager to check for the existence of a user or group.

Description: This method pre-allocates an ID based on the current principal type, delegating the actual allocation to the SecurityManager. It supports pre-allocating IDs for accounts and groups.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method retrieves a PrincipalType based on a given element name. If no PrincipalType matches the provided element name, it throws an exception.
Return value description: The PrincipalType object that corresponds to the input element name.

Description: This method stores an integer identifier within the object. This identifier is likely used to associate the object with a specific record or entity in the system.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method resets the pre-allocated identifier associated with this object.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method searches for and returns a public getter method for a specified property within a given class.
Return value description: The public getter method for the requested property, or null if no such method is found or an error occurs.

Description: This method searches a given class for a method that acts as a setter for a specified field. It constructs the expected setter method name by prefixing 'set' to the field name and then checks all public methods of the class for a case-insensitive match.
Return value description: The setter method for the given field, or null if no such method is found or an error occurs during the search.
Technique 1: Reflection: Dynamically inspects class and method information at runtime.
Technique 2: Logging: Records errors encountered during the search process.

Description: This method searches for a method within a given class that adds a property. It looks for a method named like 'add[PropertyName]' that accepts a single String parameter.
Return value description: The method returns the found 'add' method if one matches the criteria, otherwise it returns null.
Technique 1: Reflection is used to inspect class methods and their parameters.
Technique 2: Logging is used to record errors encountered during the search.

Description: This method searches for a specific public method within a given class. The target method is identified by a name constructed from the prefix "insert" followed by a provided property string, ignoring case. The method must also accept exactly two parameters: an integer and a string.
Return value description: It returns the `Method` object if a matching method is found, otherwise it returns `null`.

Description: This method attempts to configure an instance based on its class annotations and a provided configuration. It checks for the presence of a configuration annotation, retrieves the relevant configuration, and then proceeds to configure the instance using that configuration. It also includes logic to prevent a configuration from being used by multiple instances simultaneously.
Return value description: The method returns a Configuration object if the configuration and instance are successfully processed, otherwise it returns null.
Technique 1: Reflection for accessing class annotations and metadata.
Technique 2: Object referencing with WeakReference to manage instance lifecycle.
Technique 3: Logging for recording warnings and errors during the configuration process.

Description: Parses an XML input stream to create a configuration object.
Return value description: A Configuration object representing the parsed XML data.

Description: This method serializes a reference to a configurable instance into an XML format. It handles cases where the reference is null by outputting a comment, and otherwise generates an XML element with an attribute representing the reference.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method serializes a configurable instance, either by its reference or by extracting and writing its field value as an XML element. It handles cases where the instance is a reference, is not a configuration class, or the specified field is not found. It also manages null field values by emitting a comment.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.
Technique 1: Reflection is used to inspect class annotations and fields.
Technique 2: XML serialization is performed using SAX.
Technique 3: Logging is used to record errors.

Description: This method serializes a configurable object into an XML format using a SAX serializer. It processes fields annotated as attributes and elements, handling various data types including lists, maps, and nested configurable objects. Null values are skipped and commented out, and references can be specified for element attributes.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Reflection is used to access and process class fields and annotations.
Technique 2: XML serialization is performed using the SAX API.
Technique 3: Custom annotations are used to define the structure and behavior of configuration fields.

Description: This method retrieves or creates a configuration object, first checking a cache, then attempting to load it from a specified database document. If the document does not exist and the database is not in read-only mode, it attempts to save a new configuration. If the database is read-only and no configuration exists, it creates an in-memory configuration.
Return value description: Returns a Configuration object if found or successfully created, otherwise returns null.
Technique 1: Database call to load configuration from storage.
Technique 3: Serialization of configuration data to XML.

Description: This method retrieves or creates a configuration object based on a document and a broker pool. It first checks a cache for an existing configuration; if not found, it parses the document's root element to create a new configuration and then caches it.
Return value description: Returns a Configuration object if successful, otherwise returns null.

Description: This method saves a configurable instance to a database at a specified URI. It handles potential database connection issues and exceptions during the save operation.
Return value description: The saved document as a DocumentImpl object.

Description: This method saves a configurable instance to a specified XML database collection. It first retrieves the collection using the provided database broker and URI, then proceeds with the save operation. If the collection is not found or a permission error occurs during retrieval, it throws an IOException.
Return value description: Returns a DocumentImpl object representing the saved document.
Technique 1: Database call to retrieve a collection.
Technique 2: Database call to save a document.

Description: This method serializes a configurable instance into an XML string and stores it as a document within a collection in the database. It manages database transactions, acquires necessary locks, and handles security permissions during the storage process.
Return value description: The method returns the stored document object if the operation is successful, or null if the serialized data is empty. It can throw various exceptions related to I/O, configuration, security, locking, or database errors.

Description: This method clears cached configurations associated with a specific database instance. It iterates through a map of configurations, checking if a configuration's URI matches the provided database ID. If it matches, the configuration is potentially reset, and then the entry is removed from the cache.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method removes a specific configuration from a collection of hot configurations if it exists within that collection. It iterates through the existing hot configurations to find and remove the matching entry.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method adds a configuration attribute to a collection of attributes.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method adds a collection of attribute fields to an existing list of attributes.
Adds a configuration element to a collection of elements within the configurator.
Return value description: None.

Description: This method appends a collection of configuration elements to an existing list of elements.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method searches through a collection of configuration attributes and elements to find a field that matches a given annotation value.
Return value description: Returns an AField object that matches the provided annotation value, or null if no match is found.
Technique 1: Iterates through lists of configuration fields.
Technique 2: Accesses annotation values on configuration fields.

Description: This method provides a way to iterate over a collection of configuration fields, prioritizing attribute fields before element fields.
Return value description: An Iterator that allows sequential access to configuration fields.

Description: This method provides access to a reference resolver, which is a component responsible for resolving references within the system.
Return value description: The method returns an instance of the resolver.

Description: This method resolves a reference to its underlying referent object.
Return value description: The resolved referent object.

Description: This method attempts to find and invoke a specific method on a provided resolver object. It looks for a method with a given name that accepts a single String argument, and if found, it executes it and caches the result. If the method is not found or an exception occurs during invocation, the cached result remains null.
Return value description: The result of the invoked method, or null if the method was not found or an error occurred.
Technique 1: Reflection is used to dynamically inspect and invoke methods on the resolver object.
Technique 2: Method caching is employed to store the result of the method invocation for subsequent calls.

Description: This method returns the resolver instance associated with this object.
Return value description: The resolver instance.

Description: This method checks if a setting with the specified name exists within the system's configuration.
Return value description: Returns true if the setting is found, and false otherwise.

Description: This method stores an object internally, associating it with a given name. It maintains a mapping between string names and arbitrary objects.
Return value description: The object that was just added to the internal storage.

Description: This method checks a given XML document for any changes.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method saves the system's configuration. It can throw exceptions if the user lacks permission to save or if there's an issue with the configuration itself.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: Saves the current configuration settings using the provided database broker. It can throw exceptions if there are permission issues or errors within the configuration itself.
This method reclaims memory that was previously used by the cache.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method returns a string representation of the object.
Return value description: A string value.

Description: Retrieves a string representation of the value contained within this object.
Return value description: The string representation of the value.

Description: This method returns the name associated with the object.
Return value description: The name of the object as a String.

Description: This method is responsible for mapping data, likely transforming it from one format or structure to another.
Return value description: A String representing the mapped data.

Description: This method returns a string representation of the object's value.
Return value description: A string representing the value.

Description: This method extracts a value from a string based on a known key and separator.
Return value description: The extracted value from the settings string.

Description: This method determines a setting key based on a provided string, handling cases where the string might contain a key-value separator.
Return value description: Returns a SettingKey object that represents the identified setting.

Description: This method finds and returns a `SettingKey` object based on a provided string key. If no matching `SettingKey` is found, it throws an exception.
Return value description: A `SettingKey` object that corresponds to the input string key.
Technique 1: Iterates through a predefined set of possible settings.
Technique 2: Performs string comparison to find a match.

Description: This method returns a string representation of the object. It does not interact with any external systems.
Return value description: A string that represents the object.

Description: This method retrieves a string representation of the object's value.
Return value description: The string representation of the object's value.

Description: This method returns a string representation of the object's value.
Return value description: A string representing the object's value.

Description: This method creates a new Java object by dynamically loading and interpreting instructions from an XML configuration. It parses the XML to instantiate classes and invoke methods based on the defined structure.
Return value description: A newly created Java object as defined by the XML mapping instructions, or null if an error occurs during processing.
Technique 1: XML parsing using StAX (Streaming API for XML)
Technique 2: Dynamic class instantiation and method invocation via reflection (MethodHandles, LambdaMetafactory)

Description: This method attempts to dynamically invoke a method on a given object based on a configuration. It checks for the presence of required attributes, finds the matching method by name and parameter type, and then invokes it with either a pre-defined value or a value retrieved from an XML element's attribute.
Return value description: Returns true if a method was successfully found and invoked, and false otherwise.
Technique 1: Reflection is used to inspect and invoke methods on an object at runtime.
Technique 2: An object's class is inspected to find methods with a specific name.
Technique 3: Attribute values are retrieved from an XML element.

Description: This method stops all active brokers and cleans up resources. It ensures that all associated connections and services are gracefully shut down.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method serves as the entry point for the application. It validates the Java version, parses command-line arguments, and then processes these arguments. If any exceptions occur during argument parsing or processing, it handles them by printing error messages and exiting with an appropriate status code.

This is the main entry point of the application, responsible for initializing and starting the embedded Jetty server. It performs initial checks for Java version compatibility, parses command-line arguments to configure the server and application settings, and then launches the server.
Return value description: This method does not return any value as it is a void method and its primary function is to initiate the server process and manage its lifecycle, including exiting the application with appropriate status codes.

Description: This method serves as an entry point to initiate a process. It delegates the actual execution to another method, passing a boolean flag to control its behavior.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method configures and starts an embedded Jetty server. It determines the Jetty home directory, sets up logging, and resolves the appropriate configuration file based on whether it's running in a standalone mode. Finally, it initiates the Jetty server with the specified configuration.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 3: Conditional logic based on runtime arguments

Description: This method initializes and starts a server, loading configurations from specified files or a fallback location on the classpath. It configures the database instance, registers the XMLDB driver, and sets up Jetty server configurations, including various connectors and handlers. The method logs detailed startup information and notifies observers about the server's status.
Return value description: The method does not return any value.
Technique 1: File system access to load configuration files.
Technique 2: Classpath resource loading for fallback configuration.

Description: This method stops all active broker pools and waits until the system is fully stopped. It also attempts to unregister a shutdown hook if one is present.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 2: Concurrency control using waiting and notification

Description: This method initiates a graceful shutdown of a server, specifically designed to allow remaining requests to complete before stopping the server. If no instances remain, it schedules the server to stop after a one-second delay. This process involves stopping the Jetty server and ensuring its threads are joined.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method gracefully stops the server and its associated broker pool. It checks if the server is already in a stopping or stopped state before initiating the shutdown sequence.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.
Technique 1: Stops all brokers in the pool.

Description: This method signals that the server is starting. It logs the event, notifies observers about the starting status, updates the internal status to 'starting', and then notifies all threads waiting on this object.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method signals that the server has started, updates its status, and notifies any observers and waiting threads.
Return value description: void

Description: This method is called when a component in the lifecycle experiences a failure. It receives the lifecycle object and the throwable that caused the failure.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method signals that the Jetty server is in the process of stopping, updates its status to reflect this, and notifies any waiting threads. It logs an informational message indicating the server is stopping.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method signals that the server has stopped, updates its internal status to stopped, and notifies any waiting threads.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method saves raw data to an archive for backup purposes.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method forwards a start document event to a registered listener, if one exists.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method signals the end of an XML document by notifying any registered listeners. It may also propagate an SAXException if an error occurs during the process.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method handles the XML declaration, forwarding the version, encoding, and standalone attributes to the next listener in the chain.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method records the start of an XML namespace prefix mapping. It forwards this information to a subsequent listener if one exists.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method forwards the end of a prefix mapping event to the next listener in a chain, if one exists.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method forwards the start of an XML element and its attributes to a registered listener, if one exists.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method forwards the end of an XML element event to a registered listener, if one exists. This is typically part of an XML parsing process where elements are being processed sequentially.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method processes character data within an XML document, forwarding it to a registered listener if one exists.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method processes an attribute by potentially forwarding it to a next listener if one is configured.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method processes XML comments by forwarding them to a registered listener if one exists. This allows for custom handling of comments within an XML processing pipeline.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method forwards character data content to the next listener in a chain. It handles the content of CDATA sections within an XML document.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method forwards processing instructions to a registered listener, if one exists. It is part of an XML parsing process.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.

Description: This method notifies the next listener about the document type declaration, including its name, public identifier, and system identifier. This is part of the XML SAX event processing pipeline.
Return value description: This method does not return a value.
Technique 1: Callback notification to a chained listener.

Description: This method conditionally forwards a sequence of characters to another listener if one is configured. It appears to be part of a processing pipeline where text might be passed along for further handling.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method initiates the process of replacing a document within the system. It prepares for subsequent operations that will remove existing indexed data and then store new data for the document, ultimately completing the replacement via a transaction.
This method finalizes the process of replacing a document within a transaction, signaling the completion of the document replacement operation.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method initiates the indexing process for a document within the current transaction.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method processes the opening tag of an element within a database transaction, using information about the element's stored representation and its current path in the document structure.

This method is called when an attribute has been stored to the database. It takes the current transaction, the attribute that was stored, and the path of the node associated with the attribute as input.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method is called when a text node has been successfully stored in the database. It receives the transaction details, the text node itself, and the path to the node within the document.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method processes the closing tag of an XML element within a transaction, updating its stored representation in the database based on the provided element and its path.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method finalizes the storage process for a document within the current transaction.
Return value description: This method does not return any value.

Description: This method initiates a scan of a node within a database, processing its children and descendants. It utilizes a database broker to obtain an iterator for the node, retrieves the node's path, and then recursively scans the node's contents using the provided transaction and listener.
